docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Wiki
docs.text: Wonder Kingdom is a MapleStory-like open-world platformer RPG built with GameLib. This wiki covers its world, its story and everything you can find, fight and make in it.

docs.title: Where things come from
docs.text:
• Lore is written here. This wiki is the source of truth for the story, the history and the people of Wonder Kingdom.
  • Game data (items, skills, jobs, monsters, bosses, NPCs, quests, maps, professions) is generated from the game's content files in GameLib, which is the source of truth for how the game plays. Those pages are rebuilt by tools/generate.py, so fix game data in GameLib, not here.

docs.title: The Snail King
docs.text:
A giant snail named Mano sleeps in a hollow past the woods, and it does not like visitors. Watch the red marks: they show where it will land. Potions work in there; scrolls do not.

Boss Mano Arena The Snail King's Hollow
  • Unlocked by The Snail King
  • Entered by talking to Hale

docs.title: Consumables
docs.text: Item Price Description AP Reset Scroll 100 Moves one ability point from STR to DEX. It cannot take back what you started with. All Cure Potion 100 Cures poison, seal, darkness, weakness and curse. Antidote 25 Cures the state of being poisoned. Blue Potion 100 A potion made from blue herbs. Restores 100 MP. EXP Potion 100 A fantastical brew that is all learning. Gives 500 EXP. Elixir 1,500 A rare potion of legend. Restores half of your HP and MP. Eyedrop 25 Cures darkness: the world is clear again. Herb Salad 20 Fresh marjoram tossed in oil. Restores 70 MP. Holy Water 60 Allows you to recover from the state of curse or of being sealed up. Hunter's Bento 150 A packed lunch for a long day in the fields. Restores 250 HP and 100 MP, and Defense +8 for 5 minutes. Lavender Tea 60 A warm cup of lavender and rosemary. Restores 130 MP. Mandarin Dango 90 Sticky dumplings glazed with mandarin. Restores 120 HP and 80 MP, and quickens the step for 5 minutes. Mushroom Ramen 260 A rich ramen of horny mushrooms and lemon balm. Restores 400 HP and 150 MP, and Attack +4, Defense +4 for 5 minutes. Mushroom Rice Ball 35 A rice ball with a mushroom filling and a lavender leaf. Restores 90 HP. Orange Potion 80 A strong potion made from red herbs. Restores 150 HP. Red Potion 25 A potion made from red herbs. Restores 50 HP. Roast Pork 70 A pig's head roasted over firewood with rosemary. Restores 200 HP. SP Reset Scroll 100 Takes back every skill point spent on your job's attacks. They return to level 1, and the points can be spent again. Speed Potion 125 Increases speed. Speed +8 for 3 minutes. Tonic 40 Cures the state of weakness. Town Return Scroll 200 Read it to be taken back to the town this place belongs to. Use Slot Expansion Coupon 100 Adds a row of 4 slots to the Use tab, up to 96 slots. Warrior Potion 125 Increases attacking ability. Weapon Attack +5 for 3 minutes. White Potion 160 The strongest potion made from red herbs. Restores 300 HP.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Item Price Description Blue Cloth 22 Sturdy cloth woven from fern fibre and dyed blue. Blue Snail Shell 2 The blue shell of a snail. Collectors pay a little for it. Bronze Ingot 80 A bar of smelted bronze, harder than copper. Bronze Ore 15 Soft ore that a smith can turn into bronze. Copper Ingot 40 A bar of smelted copper: the first thing a smith learns to make. Copper Ore 8 Reddish ore struck from a copper vein. A smith can melt it into an ingot. Fern Fibre 6 Long tough strands stripped from a fern: stronger than plain fibre, and it takes blue dye well. Firewood 9 Good, dry firewood split from an axe-wielding stump. Green Cloth 14 Plain cloth woven from plant fibre. A tailor starts every garment from it. Green Mushroom Cap 14 The green cap of a big mushroom. Green Snail Shell 1 All that is left of a snail. Collectors pay a little for it. Herbal Ink 10 A dark ink steeped from marjoram. An alchemist brews it; a scrollcrafter writes with it. Horny Mushroom Cap 22 The spotted cap of a mushroom with a short temper. Iron Ingot 150 A bar of smelted iron, for blades and shields that last. Iron Ore 30 Heavy grey ore from an iron vein. A smith can melt it into an ingot. Lavender Flower 6 A soft pink-purple bloom from a lavender patch: calming in a potion, gentle in a pot. Lemon Balm Flower 32 A green, lemon-scented flower from a deep patch. It makes the strongest potions and dishes. Mandarin Flower 20 An orange blossom that smells of sweet peel. It strengthens a brew. Marjoram Flower 3 A small, sharp-smelling flower picked from a marjoram patch. Alchemists and cooks both want it. Mushroom Spore 3 A spore shaken from a small mushroom's cap. Orange Mushroom Cap 7 The orange cap of a mushroom, still springy. Pig's Head 10 A pig's head. A cook in town would know what to do with it. Pig's Ribbon 6 A pink ribbon a pig wore with pride. Plant Fibre 2 Dry strands pulled from a hay bale. A tailor spins them into cloth; a scribe presses them into paper. Rainbow Snail Shell 350 A shell found only through Mano. They say it is powerful enough to grant a wish. Red Cloth 18 Cloth dyed red with snail shell, for headbands and capes. Red Snail Shell 4 The red shell of a snail, harder than the blue. Rosemary Flower 12 A blue rosemary flower. Brewers use it for blue potions, cooks for roasts. Scroll Paper 5 A stiff sheet pressed from branches and fibre, ready for a scrollcrafter's ink. Tree Branch 2 A dry branch. Good for a fire, or for a crafter.

docs.title: Lore
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is a bright, prosperous and genuinely united kingdom on the island of Veligor. Its people come from different cultures and keep different traditions, yet they share a real sense of belonging and respect for one another. Their towns are lively, their markets are full, and their differences are celebrated rather than feared.

It was not always so. Before the kingdom, Veligor was split between four peoples who had fought each other for generations. Only the coming of the Balrog, an ancient being too strong for any one of them, drove them to stand together. They beat it, sealed it beneath the roots of the great World Tree, and founded Wonder Kingdom on the cooperation that won that war.

Fifty years ago, an expedition into the World Tree opened a rift deep beneath its roots and damaged the seal. The Balrog has not escaped, but its influence has been seeping out ever since. Wild creatures have grown aggressive, and the wilderness between the towns has filled with monsters.

The kingdom is still whole and happy. The land around it is turning hostile. That contrast is the heart of the world.

Core premise

Wonder Kingdom is a genuinely happy and united civilization, born from the cooperation of four formerly divided peoples. Generations later, an ancient threat imprisoned beneath the World Tree is slowly returning, and a new generation must protect the peaceful world its ancestors created.

docs.title: The Age of Disturbance
docs.text: The fifty years since the expedition are known as the Age of Disturbance. Through the damaged seal, the Balrog's influence has been creeping out of its prison and across Veligor, and its effects grow harder to ignore every year. Above all, the island's wilderness has become far more dangerous.

docs.title: Wild Creatures Turn Aggressive
docs.text:
Creatures that once kept away from travelers, or simply went about their lives, began attacking anyone who wandered into their territory. Monsters became common in the forests, plains, mountains and caves.

It is not the same everywhere. Some places have seen only small changes, while others have become home to truly dangerous creatures. The towns themselves are still peaceful, but every road between them has grown riskier.

docs.title: The Nature of Monsters
docs.text:
The monsters roaming Veligor are tied to the weakening seal. The spread of the Balrog's influence is why such a peaceful land is now full of hostile creatures.

That does not mean the Balrog commands every one of them. Some are ordinary animals whose nature it has twisted. Others are magical beings changed by a changing land.

docs.title: Life Under the Disturbance
docs.text:
The growing danger in the wilds has made travel, exploration, farming and any work outside the towns harder. Yet Wonder Kingdom carries on. Its towns are still prosperous and welcoming, and its people work together against the threat.

The kingdom has not fallen into fear, hostility or division. The monsters are simply a new challenge, met by a civilization that was already united.

Design notes

"The Age of Disturbance" is a provisional name. Exactly how the Balrog's influence creates or changes monsters is not settled, including whether entirely new creatures can appear.

docs.title: The Balrog
docs.text:
The Balrog is the greatest threat Wonder Kingdom has ever faced. It is an ancient being of immense power and destruction, which once nearly destroyed every people on Veligor, and which now lies imprisoned beneath the World Tree, held by a seal that is slowly failing.

To most people today, it is a legend: a monster from history books and bedtime stories. To the guardians of Cavelor, it is the reason their city exists.

docs.title: What It Is
docs.text:
No one alive has seen the Balrog, and the old accounts disagree about almost everything. They agree on a few things:

  • It is enormous, larger than any creature on Veligor, and it moved through the land like a storm.
  • It burned. Settlements it passed were left as ash, and the ground where it stood stayed scorched for years.
  • It could not be killed. The four peoples' greatest warriors wounded it again and again, and every wound closed.
  • Its influence spreads. Even before it reached a place, the creatures there grew wild and vicious, as if something in them had answered it.

Beyond that, every people tells it differently. Savage songs describe a horned giant wreathed in flame. Magician records describe it as something less like an animal and more like a wound in the world, a hunger given shape. Commons tales call it simply "the Burning". Aristocrat chronicles, which care about numbers, record the armies and towns it destroyed, and say little about what it was.

docs.title: Where It Came From
docs.text:
The oldest question about the Balrog has never been answered. The four peoples each have a story:

  • The Savages say it came out of the deep earth, woken from a sleep older than the island by the noise of their endless wars.
  • The Magicians believe it came from somewhere else entirely, through a tear in the world, drawn by the World Tree's magic the way moths are drawn to a lantern.
  • The Commons say it was always there, under the island, and that the island's warmth and fertility are what is left over from its fire.
  • The Aristocrats recorded only that it appeared in the far wilds and moved toward the center of Veligor, toward the World Tree, from the very first day.

No one knows which, if any, is true. Cavelor's scholars say that each story might hold a piece of the truth.

docs.title: The First Burning
docs.text:
The Balrog first appeared in the wilds at the edge of Veligor, while the Age of Division still raged. Its first victims were frontier villages of both alliances. Each side blamed the other at first, and wasted precious time accusing each other of some terrible new weapon.

By the time they understood, it was moving inland. Armies sent against it were scattered. Strongholds that had held for generations against human enemies burned in a night. Refugees from all four peoples fled toward the center of the island, and the Balrog followed, always moving toward the World Tree.

docs.title: The Alliance
docs.text:
With the Balrog closing on the heart of the island, the four peoples finally met under truce. It was the first time in generations that their leaders had sat at one table. The talks were bitter and nearly failed more than once, but the refugee camps filling the plains made the choice for them. They united.

Each people gave what it did best. The Savages sent their strongest warriors. The Magicians brought their knowledge of ancient magic. The Commons supplied, armed and fed the united army. The Aristocrats organized it and commanded it as one.

docs.title: The Last Stand at the Tree
docs.text:
The final battle was fought at the foot of the World Tree. The united army could not kill the Balrog, but it could hold it and wear it down, and that was the plan: while the warriors fought, the Magicians worked a seal powerful enough to bind it forever.

The battle lasted for days. The Savage front line held the Balrog in place, at terrible cost. When the creature finally weakened enough, the Magicians drove it down into the earth beneath the Tree and closed the seal over it, binding it deep within the roots.

The war was over. The four peoples who had fought together founded Wonder Kingdom, and a company of warriors stayed below to guard the seal. Their descendants are the people of Cavelor.

docs.title: The Seal
docs.text:
The seal is a binding of powerful magic, made by the Magicians and strengthened by the combined efforts of the whole alliance. It holds the Balrog in a prison deep below the World Tree, beneath Cavelor and the oldest roots.

For the whole history of the kingdom, it held. Then, fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition accidentally opened a rift in the deep passages near the prison and damaged it. The seal did not break, but it began to weaken, and it has been weakening ever since.

docs.title: The Balrog Today
docs.text:
Through the damaged seal, the Balrog's influence has been seeping out across Veligor. This is the cause of the Age of Disturbance: creatures grown aggressive, monsters filling the wilds, and danger on every road between the towns. It is exactly what the old accounts described happening before the Balrog arrived, and that is what worries Cavelor's guardians most.

What the Balrog wants, whether it is aware of the world above, and what will happen if the seal fails completely, nobody knows.

Design notes

The Balrog's true nature, intentions and fate are deliberately undecided (principle 16). The four peoples' stories about its origin are legends inside the world, not established fact. New with this page: the first appearance in the far wilds, the First Burning, the truce talks, the Last Stand at the Tree with the Savage front line holding the Balrog while the Magicians worked the seal, and the Balrog always moving toward the World Tree.

docs.title: The Great World Tree Expedition
docs.text: Fifty years ago, Wonder Kingdom sent an expedition into the World Tree. The Tree had been a landmark for centuries, but most of its interior had never been explored, and the journey became one of the greatest feats of exploration in the kingdom's history.

docs.title: The Upper Chambers
docs.text:
The explorers first climbed up through the Tree's vast inner passages. They found astonishing magical places: strange plants, extraordinary creatures and natural structures of dizzying complexity.

There they met the Children of the Tree, a magical people who had lived cut off from the rest of the world. After the expedition, the Children gradually moved to Fairy Forest and became part of the wider kingdom.

docs.title: The Discovery of Cavelor
docs.text:
Having explored the heights, the expedition turned downward, into the depths beneath the Tree. There they found Cavelor.

They learned that the descendants of ancient guardians had lived in the hidden city for generations, keeping the memory of the Balrog alive and guarding its prison. The legendary war against the Balrog, it turned out, had left behind a living order sworn to stop its return.

docs.title: The Accident
docs.text:
Exploring the passages deeper still, the explorers accidentally opened a rift, and the rift damaged the magic that held the Balrog.

The seal did not break. It began, very slowly, to weaken. At first nobody realized what had happened. But over the following decades, the failing seal began to reach the world above, and the Age of Disturbance began.

docs.title: The Age of Division
docs.text: Long before Wonder Kingdom, four peoples shared Veligor, and each had its own idea of how life ought to be lived.

docs.title: The Savages
docs.text: The Savages held the rugged wilds and the mountains. They prized strength, endurance and independence, honored their ancestors, and lived close to the land. Their communities were built around survival and cooperation, and respect went to whoever showed courage and perseverance. They fought off every outside authority that tried to rule their territory or press strange customs on them.

docs.title: The Magicians
docs.text: The Magicians gave their lives to understanding the supernatural forces of Veligor, above all the World Tree, the old places where magic ran deep, and the bond between magic and nature. They valued knowledge, magical skill and preservation, and they stood against anyone who tried to exploit or seize the places they held sacred.

docs.title: The Commons
docs.text: The Commons were the farmers, merchants, craftsmen and settlers who kept ordinary life running. They built villages, farms, workshops and trade routes, and they valued cooperation, practical skill, honest work and prosperity. What they wanted most was safety and stability across the island.

docs.title: The Aristocrats
docs.text: The Aristocrats raised fortified settlements, wrote laws and built the first real institutions of government. They believed that order, administration and strong central leadership were the way to a stable and prosperous Veligor.

docs.title: The Ancient Conflict
docs.text:
For generations the island was split into two loose alliances: the Savages and the Magicians on one side, the Commons and the Aristocrats on the other.

They fought over land, over who had the right to rule, over whose traditions should prevail, and over access to the island's most important natural and magical places. The quarrels hardened into long wars. Each side had real strengths, but neither could win a lasting peace, and Veligor never became one civilization.

It took a far greater threat to end it.

docs.title: The Balrog War
docs.text:
The ancient conflict was cut short by the arrival of the Balrog, a being of immense power and destruction.

It threatened every people on the island at once. Settlements burned, armies were broken, and even the mightiest warriors and magicians could barely stand against it. For the first time, all four peoples faced an enemy none of them could beat alone, and next to that danger their old grievances suddenly seemed very small.

So they united, and each gave what it did best:

  • The Savages sent their strongest warriors, whose courage and strength carried the fight to the Balrog itself.
  • The Magicians brought their knowledge of ancient magic, which in the end made it possible to imprison the creature.
  • The Commons gathered supplies, forged equipment and kept the united armies fed and moving.
  • The Aristocrats supplied military organization and leadership, and coordinated the four forces as one.

Together they defeated the Balrog. But it could not be destroyed. Instead, the alliance wove a great magical seal and bound the creature deep within the roots of the World Tree at the heart of Veligor.

That victory ended the Age of Division.

docs.title: The Founding of Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
After the Balrog was sealed away, the leaders of the four peoples met to make the peace last. They signed a treaty that formally ended their old wars and joined them into a single realm: Wonder Kingdom.

The founding treaty declared that every people of Veligor could live together in peace, whatever their ancestry, culture, station or magical gifts. The kingdom was built on the same cooperation that had won the war.

Over the generations that followed, the four peoples grew a shared identity without giving up their own. Their cultures kept living and changing inside the new kingdom. Towns traded, friendships crossed the old lines, and knowledge passed freely from one community to the next. The old hostilities faded until nobody thought of their neighbors as ancestral enemies anymore. The unity the treaty had promised simply became the way people lived.

docs.title: The Meaning of Unity
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is not held together by fear, force or a fragile political bargain. Its unity is real.

Its people understand and value one another across their differences. Each town keeps its own customs and way of life, and those differences are a source of pride rather than friction. Everyone is proud of the shared history and of the civilization their ancestors built. The old wars are remembered as history, but they no longer shape how communities treat each other.

That holds for every settlement on Veligor, including Urbanograd, whose unconventional culture is accepted across the kingdom.

docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Today
docs.text:
Fifty years have passed since the Great World Tree Expedition, and Wonder Kingdom is still peaceful, prosperous and wonderfully diverse.

  • Selsior flourishes as the bustling capital.
  • Kaldemor keeps its cheerful country traditions and its love of craft.
  • Midbarium holds fast to its resilient highland ways.
  • Fairy Forest remains the heart of magic and harmony with nature.
  • Urbanograd, now a century old, still goes its own colorful way.
  • Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour thrive as independent ports with very different characters.
  • Cavelor keeps its ancient watch beneath the World Tree.

docs.title: Everyday Life
docs.text:
For all the danger beyond their walls, the people of Wonder Kingdom live ordinary, happy lives. They trade, farm, craft, learn, play, explore and celebrate. Travel, trade, friendship and shared culture tie the island's communities together, and people are proud to call the kingdom home.

Their happiness is real. It is not a pretty face hiding a broken society.

docs.title: The Dangerous Wilderness
docs.text:
Outside the towns, it is another story. Monsters roam much of Veligor's wilderness, and forests, mountains, plains, caves and ancient ruins have all grown more dangerous. Travelers and adventurers must face aggressive creatures and treacherous ground.

Peaceful towns and a dangerous wild: that contrast is the defining feature of the world.

docs.title: The Forgotten Threat
docs.text:
To most people, the Balrog is a legend, a figure out of history books. It was defeated and locked away so long ago that hardly anyone thinks of it as a danger today.

The people of Cavelor know better. They remember the first war and understand the seal, and they know that its slow failure is a serious threat.

And deep beneath the World Tree, the Balrog's influence keeps spreading.

docs.title: Worldbuilding Principles
docs.text:
These principles guide all future lore. New pages and stories should stay true to them.

  1. Wonder Kingdom is genuinely united. Its communities are not secretly hostile toward one another.
  2. The four original peoples were once divided. Their conflict ended through cooperation against the Balrog and the founding treaty that followed.
  3. Cultural differences still matter. Unity did not erase the traditions or identities of Veligor's communities.
  4. Urbanograd was founded 100 years ago. Its people are rebels in a cultural sense, not political insurgents.
  5. Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour are independent towns. Their resemblance to other towns is cultural and atmospheric, not a sign that anyone governs them.
  6. Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour lie on opposite sides of Veligor. They have different identities without being rivals.
  7. Selsior is the City of Everything. It is a joyful, bustling, cosmopolitan metropolis with classic medieval fantasy architecture.
  8. Kaldemor is the Town of Joyful Craftsmanship. It is a cheerful, prosperous, pastoral community inspired by Henesys.
  9. Midbarium is a rugged, rural highland town of four families. Each family chooses its chieftain, and together they choose the Old One who leads them all. It stands for strength, resilience, independence and ancestral tradition, and its dry, desert-like highlands draw on highland, canyon and steppe cultures, not Middle Eastern ones.
  10. Fairy Forest is a magical woodland town. It is the Magicians' historic home and the new home of the Children of the Tree.
  11. Cavelor was founded by ancient guardians. Its people still carry the duty of watching over the Balrog's prison.
  12. The Great World Tree Expedition took place 50 years ago. It found the Children of the Tree and Cavelor, and accidentally damaged the Balrog's seal.
  13. The weakening seal makes the wilderness ever more dangerous. This is the core explanation for the aggressive monsters across Veligor.
  14. The kingdom stays peaceful despite the monsters. The danger is in the land and the wilds, not between its peoples.
  15. The player belongs to Wonder Kingdom from the start. The player character was born and raised here.
  16. The Balrog is the overarching ancient threat. Its true nature, intentions and fate are not yet fully decided.
  17. The world is mostly bright, colorful, prosperous and adventurous. Dark places and dangerous creatures exist, but they do not define everyday life in the kingdom.
  18. Not every story is about the Balrog. The world has ordinary lives, personal adventures, local traditions and mysteries of its own.
  19. Veligor is the starting point, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may come later.
  20. Undecided details stay undecided. New lore should be clear about what is established and what is only a proposal, rather than quietly adding new canon. On these pages, open questions are kept in Design notes boxes.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: When What happened The ancient era The four peoples build their own civilizations across Veligor. The Age of Division The Savages and Magicians fight the Commons and Aristocrats for generations. The Balrog War The Balrog appears in the far wilds and burns its way toward the World Tree. The four peoples unite and make their last stand at the foot of the Tree. The Founding The Balrog is defeated and sealed beneath the World Tree. The founding treaty creates Wonder Kingdom, and guardians stay below to found Cavelor. The Age of Unity The kingdom prospers, its towns grow, and the old divisions fade away. 100 years ago The Walkers leave Selsior and settle the ruins of Old Grad, founding Urbanograd. The Open Charter recognizes it as a town of the kingdom. 50 years ago The Great World Tree Expedition finds the Children of the Tree and Cavelor. 50 years ago The expedition accidentally opens a rift that damages the Balrog's seal. The following decades The Age of Disturbance: the Balrog's influence spreads, and the wilderness grows ever more dangerous. Today Wonder Kingdom is united and prosperous, monsters roam much of the wilderness, and the Balrog's prison keeps weakening.

docs.title: Veligor
docs.text:
Veligor is a large island and the home of Wonder Kingdom. Its land is wonderfully varied: fertile plains, high mountains, enchanted forests, long coastlines, quiet farmland, ancient ruins, deep caverns and wide stretches of wilderness.

Near its center rises the enormous World Tree, visible from much of the island and one of its best-known landmarks.

Roads, footpaths and trade routes link the island's towns. The wilds between them have grown dangerous, but the towns themselves are as lively, busy and prosperous as ever, and each has a character all its own.

docs.title: Towns
docs.text:
Town Known as Character Selsior The City of Everything The bustling, joyful capital Kaldemor The Town of Joyful Craftsmanship A cheerful pastoral town of makers and farmers Midbarium The Highland Settlement A rural highland town of four families, led by the Old One Fairy Forest The Magical Woodland A forest settlement with Magician roots Urbanograd The Town of Societal Rebels A century-old home of free spirits Bain Harbour The Coastal Town A lively, prosperous port Goa Harbour The Wilderness Harbour A rustic port on the far coast Cavelor The Underground City of Guardians The hidden city beneath the World Tree

Beyond Veligor

Veligor is where the story begins, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may appear later.

docs.title: The World Tree
docs.text: At the heart of Veligor stands the World Tree, one of the island's great landmarks in every sense: geographic, historical and magical. It is no ordinary tree. Its size is staggering, and inside it lie vast worlds of their own, reaching both up into its crown and down into the earth.

docs.title: The Upper World Tree
docs.text:
High in the Tree lie great chambers, ancient branches, strange magical plants and whole ecosystems found nowhere else, home to wondrous magical creatures.

This was the home of the Children of the Tree. The people of the surface knew almost nothing of them until the expedition fifty years ago. Since then, many of the Children have moved to Fairy Forest.

docs.title: The Lower World Tree
docs.text:
Below the ground, the Tree's roots run deep, carving passages through ancient caverns and buried places. The hidden city of Cavelor lies down here.

Deeper still is the Balrog's prison.

docs.title: The Ancient Seal
docs.text:
When the four united peoples defeated the Balrog, they bound it beneath the World Tree with a seal made from powerful magic and the combined strength of the whole alliance. For generations it held.

So the World Tree has two faces. It is a source of natural beauty, magical wonder and extraordinary life, and in its deepest roots it holds the greatest ancient danger Wonder Kingdom has ever known.

docs.title: Quenna
docs.text:
Harbour Master

Role: Ruler · Age: Adult

Brisk, loud and quick to laugh, with a sailor's habit of deciding things before the tide turns. She listens to everyone at the council table and then says exactly what she thinks.

Quenna chairs the harbour council of captains, shipwrights and merchants, who chose her from among themselves. She sails her own boat in the summer race around Veligor against Goa Harbour and has never once admitted that the other side might win.

Relationships:

  • Ambrose: husband
  • Jowan: son
  • Corwin: trusted council captain
  • Ottilie: clerk
  • Mabyn: friend
  • Dunstan: race boatbuilder
  • Marisol: council ally
  • Iska: rival racer and friend
  • Tobin: trading partner

docs.title: Ottilie
docs.text:
Clerk of the Harbour Hall

Role: Official · Age: Adult

Precise, tidy and fond of rules, but kinder than her ledgers suggest. She keeps a jar of sweets for anyone who fills in a form correctly.

Ottilie records every ship that comes and goes, every cargo and every council decision. She has noticed that fewer small boats go out past the headland each year, and she is not sure who she should tell.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: employer

docs.title: Mabyn
docs.text:
Keeper of the Hall Door

Role: Service · Age: Elder

Gentle, chatty and endlessly fond of the old stories. She treats every visitor as if they had come all this way just to see her.

Mabyn opens and closes the harbour hall and polishes Old Bain's boat-hook above the door every morning. She knows more tales of Old Bain than anyone and is sure at least half of them are true.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: friend

docs.title: Jowan
docs.text:
Harbour Watchman

Role: Guard · Age: Young

Eager, earnest and a little too proud of his new coat. He salutes people who do not expect it.

Jowan joined the Harbour Watch last spring and wants very badly to prove he did not get the post because his mother is Harbour Master. He would rather be crewing in the summer race than walking the docks at night.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: mother
  • Ambrose: father
  • Halloran: commander
  • Brisa: friendly rival

docs.title: Corwin
docs.text:
Captain of the Heron

Role: Council · Age: Adult

Calm, dry and slow to speak, the kind of captain who never raises his voice because he never needs to. He hates waste and loves a good argument.

Corwin sits on the harbour council and has run cargo along the coast for twenty years without losing a crate. He now pays adventurers to sail with every voyage and grumbles about the cost at every council meeting.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: council chair
  • Annis: council rival
  • Caspian: nephew
  • Tristram: hired harpooner

docs.title: Annis
docs.text:
Captain of the Saltlark

Role: Council · Age: Elder

Weathered, blunt and superstitious, with a ritual for everything from casting off to tying her boots. She trusts the sea more than people, and people only a little.

Annis is the oldest captain on the harbour council and remembers when the bay was as calm as a millpond. She says the water has changed since the Disturbance began and wants the council to take it seriously before something goes wrong.

Relationships:

  • Corwin: council rival
  • Morwenna: sailor
  • Thaddeus: old racing rival

docs.title: Morwenna
docs.text:
Sailor of the Saltlark

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Cheerful, tough and always singing under her breath. She misses home as soon as she leaves and misses the sea as soon as she is home.

Morwenna has sailed with Captain Annis for twelve years. On her last voyage something large brushed the Saltlark's keel in deep water, and she has not told her mother or her son.

Relationships:

  • Ysolde: mother
  • Ossie: son
  • Annis: captain

docs.title: Seraphine
docs.text:
Captain of the Bright Morrow

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Bold, restless and fond of a grand gesture. She never turns down a dare and rarely turns down a contract.

Seraphine runs the fastest trading ship in the harbour and has seen more of the new creatures in the deep water than any other captain. She will not describe what she saw, but she now sails with hired adventurers on every trip and pays them well.

Relationships:

  • Barnaby: bosun
  • Keziah: hired sword

docs.title: Barnaby
docs.text:
Bosun of the Bright Morrow

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Big, booming and soft-hearted, with a story for every scar. No one is sure how many of his stories are true.

Barnaby swears that a pair of eyes as large as cartwheels looked up at him from under the Bright Morrow one moonlit night. The waterfront laughs at him, but he has not slept on deck since.

Relationships:

  • Seraphine: captain
  • Finch: devoted listener

docs.title: Tristram
docs.text:
Harpooner

Role: Adventurer · Age: Adult

Patient, still and serious, a man who can wait for hours without moving. He laughs rarely but completely.

Tristram hunted big fish until the Disturbance, and now captains hire him to stand at the bow with his harpoon in deep water. He wants to know what is down there before anyone else does.

Relationships:

  • Keziah: adventuring partner
  • Nerissa: sweetheart
  • Corwin: employer

docs.title: Lowen
docs.text:
Deckhand

Role: Worker · Age: Young

Restless, good-natured and too eager to please. He blushes when anyone praises him.

Lowen has just signed on to his first trading voyage, against his father's wishes. He hopes to earn a place on the race crew this summer.

Relationships:

  • Gwennol: mother
  • Cobb: father
  • Bree: sister
  • Thaddeus: self-appointed coach
  • Caspian: friend

docs.title: Garrow
docs.text:
Dock Foreman

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Loud, fair and always in a hurry. He knows exactly how long it takes to unload any ship and gets cross when it takes longer.

Garrow runs the dock crews and keeps cargo moving from ship to warehouse. He would like the council to build a second pier, and he raises it every chance he gets.

Relationships:

  • Tully: dockworker
  • Hobart: old friend
  • Finch: errand runner

docs.title: Tully
docs.text:
Dockworker

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Strong, easygoing and always hungry. He thinks every problem looks smaller after lunch.

Tully has carried crates on the docks since he was a boy. He is saving every coin he can to buy a small boat of his own.

Relationships:

  • Garrow: foreman

docs.title: Hobart
docs.text:
Warehouseman

Role: Worker · Age: Elder

Methodical, dry and slightly deaf in one ear, which he uses to his advantage. He trusts his own counting over anyone's ledger.

Hobart has kept the harbour warehouses for longer than Garrow has been alive. He claims some of the oldest crates in the back have been there since Old Bain's day.

Relationships:

  • Garrow: old friend

docs.title: Caspian
docs.text:
Navigator of the Heron

Role: Worker · Age: Young

Confident, clever and a bit vain about his star-reckoning. He is secretly afraid of storms.

Caspian is Captain Corwin's nephew and the youngest navigator in the harbour. He hopes to be chosen as navigator for this summer's race.

Relationships:

  • Corwin: uncle
  • Lowen: friend

docs.title: Finch
docs.text:
Errand Runner

Role: Child · Age: Child

Cheeky, quick and always knows the latest news first. He would rather run than walk anywhere.

Finch runs messages up and down the docks for a copper a time. He has heard the sailors' stories about the deep water and wants to see a sea creature with his own eyes.

Relationships:

  • Garrow: employer
  • Maren: teacher
  • Barnaby: storyteller

docs.title: Dunstan
docs.text:
Master Shipwright

Role: Council · Age: Elder

Gruff, stubborn and secretly sentimental. He talks to the ships he builds and claims they answer.

Dunstan has built more hulls than anyone alive in Bain Harbour and speaks for the shipwrights on the harbour council. He is building a new boat for this summer's race and will not let anyone, not even the Harbour Master, see the plans.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: race skipper
  • Alwyn: son
  • Kit: grandson
  • Peregrine: apprentice

docs.title: Alwyn
docs.text:
Shipwright

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult

Cheerful, steady and good with his hands, he whistles while he works and never loses his temper. He finds his father's stubbornness exhausting and admires it anyway.

Alwyn will take over the shipyard from his father one day and already does most of the heavy work. He would like to build sturdier hulls for the deep water, but Dunstan says the old designs were good enough for Old Bain.

Relationships:

  • Dunstan: father
  • Bryony: wife
  • Kit: son
  • Poppy: daughter
  • Tegan: friend

docs.title: Kit
docs.text:
Shipwright's Son

Role: Child · Age: Child

Noisy, fearless and always covered in sawdust. He can tie fourteen knots and will show you all of them.

Kit spends every spare hour at the shipyard with his father and grandfather. He has secretly carved his name inside the hull of the new race boat.

Relationships:

  • Alwyn: father
  • Bryony: mother
  • Poppy: sister
  • Dunstan: grandfather
  • Maren: teacher

docs.title: Peregrine
docs.text:
Shipwright's Apprentice

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Clever, clumsy and full of ideas, about one in ten of them good. He talks fast when he is nervous.

Peregrine is in his second year as Dunstan's apprentice. He has a plan for a faster hull that he is sure would win the summer race, if only the old man would look at it.

Relationships:

  • Dunstan: mentor

docs.title: Tegan
docs.text:
Sailmaker

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult · Sells: Sails, canvas and patching

Brisk, practical and a little sharp, with a needle always tucked behind her ear. She judges a ship by its stitching.

Tegan has sewn sails for half the ships in the harbour. She has been asked to make new sails for the race boat in secret, and she is enjoying the secret very much.

Relationships:

  • Alwyn: friend

docs.title: Gwennol
docs.text:
Fishmonger

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Fresh fish, smoked fish and crab

Loud, quick-witted and generous, with a voice that carries across the whole fish market. She can gut a fish faster than you can name it.

Gwennol's family has sold fish in Bain Harbour since it was just a cove. Her catches have grown smaller and stranger since the Disturbance, and she has started throwing back fish she does not recognise.

Relationships:

  • Cobb: husband
  • Bree: daughter
  • Lowen: son
  • Hesketh: rival stallholder

docs.title: Cobb
docs.text:
Fisherman

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Quiet, steady and soft-spoken, he lets his wife do the talking and seems happy about it. He knows every rock in the bay.

Cobb fishes the bay in a little boat his grandfather built. Twice this year his nets came up torn clean through, and he wants to know what did it before he takes his son out deeper.

Relationships:

  • Gwennol: wife
  • Bree: daughter
  • Lowen: son
  • Wenna: mother

docs.title: Bree
docs.text:
Fishmonger's Daughter

Role: Child · Age: Child

Bossy, bright and absolutely fearless around anything with claws. She names every crab she catches.

Bree helps at her mother's stall and runs a small business selling crab shells to other children. She wants to sail in the summer race more than anything in the world.

Relationships:

  • Gwennol: mother
  • Cobb: father
  • Lowen: brother
  • Wenna: grandmother

docs.title: Hesketh
docs.text:
Oyster Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Elder · Sells: Oysters, cockles and mussels

Grumpy, sly and secretly very kind. He complains about everything and gives away more oysters than he sells.

Hesketh has had the stall next to Gwennol's for thirty years and they have argued every single day of it. He feeds the harbour cat better than he feeds himself.

Relationships:

  • Gwennol: rival stallholder
  • Barnacle: favourite cat

docs.title: Wenna
docs.text:
Net-Mender

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Sharp-tongued, proud and quick with her fingers. She knows everyone's business and approves of very little of it.

Wenna mends nets on the fish market steps as she has done all her life. She says the tears in her son's nets are not the work of any fish she ever knew.

Relationships:

  • Cobb: son
  • Bree: granddaughter

docs.title: Nerissa
docs.text:
Pearl Diver

Role: Worker · Age: Young

Fearless, quiet and happiest underwater. She speaks in short sentences, as if saving her breath.

Nerissa dives for pearls and shellfish beyond the harbour wall. On her last dive she saw something move in the dark below the reef, and she has not gone back down since, though she will not say why.

Relationships:

  • Tristram: sweetheart

docs.title: Barnacle
docs.text:
Harbour Cat

Role: Animal · Age: Adult

Lazy, greedy and dignified. She sleeps in the sun on the fish market steps and accepts tribute from all who pass.

Barnacle belongs to nobody and to everybody. The fishmongers say she will not go near the water's edge since the Disturbance began, and that she is smarter than all of them.

Relationships:

  • Hesketh: feeder

docs.title: Ysolde
docs.text:
Keeper of the Light

Role: Service · Age: Elder

Solitary, wry and clear-sighted, she counts ships the way other people count sheep. She has opinions about every captain in the harbour and shares them freely.

Ysolde has kept the lighthouse lit for forty years. From the top of the tower she has seen pale lights moving under the water far out past the headland, on nights when there should be nothing there at all.

Relationships:

  • Morwenna: daughter
  • Ossie: grandson
  • Clemence: friend

docs.title: Ossie
docs.text:
Lighthouse Boy

Role: Child · Age: Child

Curious, solemn and full of questions he asks one at a time. He climbs the lighthouse stairs faster than anyone.

Ossie lives at the lighthouse with his grandmother while his mother is at sea. He has decided he will be a lighthouse keeper too, and has already started his own logbook of ships and birds.

Relationships:

  • Morwenna: mother
  • Ysolde: grandmother
  • Maren: teacher

docs.title: Halloran
docs.text:
Captain of the Harbour Watch

Role: Guard · Age: Adult

Steady, warm and hard to surprise. He settles most trouble with a hand on the shoulder and a mug of something hot.

Halloran keeps the peace on the waterfront, which mostly means sorting out arguments between sailors and tired dockworkers. Lately he has started posting a watch on the outer pier at night, and he will only say it is a precaution.

Relationships:

  • Delphine: sister
  • Brisa: watchwoman
  • Jowan: watchman

docs.title: Brisa
docs.text:
Harbour Watchwoman

Role: Guard · Age: Young

Sharp, fast and impatient, with a quick tongue and quicker feet. She can outrun anyone on the waterfront and likes to prove it.

Brisa joined the Harbour Watch because it was the best way to see everything that happens in town. She is keeping a list of strange things the sailors report and hopes someone important will read it one day.

Relationships:

  • Halloran: commander
  • Jowan: friendly rival

docs.title: Keziah
docs.text:
Sword for Hire

Role: Adventurer · Age: Young

Cool, careful and quietly funny. She counts exits when she walks into a room.

Keziah came to Bain Harbour from inland when she heard the captains were paying adventurers to sail with them. She gets terribly seasick and has told no one, least of all her employer.

Relationships:

  • Seraphine: employer
  • Tristram: adventuring partner
  • Clemence: healer

docs.title: Wilmot
docs.text:
Ropemaker

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder

Slow, kind and endlessly patient, he believes any problem can be solved with the right knot. He hums sea songs older than anyone else remembers.

Wilmot has walked his rope walk on the waterfront for fifty years. He worries that no young person in town wants to learn his trade.

Relationships:

  • Merriwether: customer

docs.title: Merriwether
docs.text:
Ship's Chandler

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Rope, tar, lanterns, hooks and ship's stores

Fussy, friendly and very fond of lists. He can find anything in his crowded shop in under a minute.

Merriwether supplies every ship that leaves the harbour. Lately captains ask him for things he has never stocked before, like heavier chain and harpoon heads, and he is trying to work out where to get them.

Relationships:

  • Wilmot: supplier

docs.title: Delphine
docs.text:
Innkeeper of the Salt and Bread

Role: Service · Age: Adult · Sells: Hot meals, ale and rooms by the night

Generous, sharp and unflappable, she can quiet a room of sailors with one look. She never forgets a debt or a kindness.

Delphine runs the busiest inn on the waterfront, where the sailors gather to swap tales of what they saw at sea. She has started writing the strangest tales down, because she thinks someone ought to.

Relationships:

  • Halloran: brother
  • Lorcan: singer at her inn
  • Bryony: baker

docs.title: Lorcan
docs.text:
Shanty Singer

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Dramatic, charming and terrible with money. He can make a whole inn sing along by the second verse.

Lorcan sings at the Salt and Bread most nights. He is writing a new shanty about the summer race and needs Bain Harbour to win so he can finish it properly.

Relationships:

  • Delphine: employer

docs.title: Clemence
docs.text:
Harbour Healer

Role: Healer · Age: Adult · Sells: Salves, bandages and seasickness tonic

Calm, practical and gently teasing. She has seen every kind of injury a ship can cause and is unimpressed by most of them.

Clemence patches up sailors, dockworkers and the occasional adventurer. Lately she has treated stings and scrapes she cannot explain, and she keeps careful notes on each one.

Relationships:

  • Ysolde: friend
  • Keziah: secret patient

docs.title: Thaddeus
docs.text:
Retired Captain

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Grand, nostalgic and fond of his own voice. He tells the same stories often but tells them well.

Thaddeus lost the summer race around Veligor by a boat's length more than thirty years ago and has never stopped talking about it. He spends his days on a bench by the water, coaching young sailors who did not ask.

Relationships:

  • Lowen: reluctant pupil
  • Annis: old racing rival

docs.title: Ambrose
docs.text:
Chartmaker

Role: Scholar · Age: Adult · Sells: Sea charts, tide tables and coastal maps

Quiet, patient and fond of tiny handwriting. He apologises to his ink when he spills it.

Ambrose draws the charts every captain in the harbour sails by. Since the Disturbance the captains keep bringing him marks for places where something was seen in the water, and he has started a separate chart for them that he keeps locked in a drawer.

Relationships:

  • Quenna: wife
  • Jowan: son
  • Poppy: admirer

docs.title: Marisol
docs.text:
Spice Merchant

Role: Council · Age: Adult · Sells: Spices, dyes and teas from all over the island

Charming, sharp-eyed and impossible to haggle down. She remembers the name of every customer's child.

Marisol speaks for the merchants on the harbour council. Her goods come by sea from every corner of Veligor, and lately some cargoes have arrived late or not at all, which worries her more than she lets anyone see.

Relationships:

  • Cordelia: business partner
  • Quenna: council ally

docs.title: Bryony
docs.text:
Baker of Merchant Street

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Bread, salt rolls and sailors' hard biscuits

Warm, busy and up before the sun. She feeds anyone who looks hungry whether they pay or not.

Bryony's bakery is why Bain Harbour smells of fresh bread in the morning. She bakes the hard biscuits every ship takes to sea and hopes her children will grow up to like flour more than salt water.

Relationships:

  • Alwyn: husband
  • Kit: son
  • Poppy: daughter
  • Delphine: customer

docs.title: Poppy
docs.text:
Baker's Daughter

Role: Child · Age: Child

Shy, thoughtful and fond of drawing. She notices things grown-ups miss.

Poppy delivers bread along Merchant Street every morning and sketches the ships in the bay. She wants to make maps like Ambrose one day.

Relationships:

  • Alwyn: father
  • Bryony: mother
  • Kit: brother
  • Ambrose: mentor

docs.title: Cordelia
docs.text:
Cloth Merchant

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Woollens, oilskins and bright cloth

Elegant, cheerful and a born gossip. She dresses better than anyone in town and wants everyone to know it.

Cordelia buys cloth from inland towns and sells it to sailors and townsfolk alike. She is Marisol's business partner and dreams of opening a second shop.

Relationships:

  • Marisol: business partner

docs.title: Maren
docs.text:
Harbour Schoolteacher

Role: Scholar · Age: Adult

Patient, bright and strict about spelling. She can make a lesson out of anything that washes up on the beach.

Maren teaches the harbour children their letters, their sums and the names of the stars. She is trying to get the council to pay for a proper schoolhouse.

Relationships:

  • Kit: pupil
  • Finch: pupil
  • Ossie: pupil

docs.title: People of Cavelor
docs.text: The 15 people of Cavelor in the game's first release.

docs.title: Leaders
docs.text: • Marrun, Keeper of the Oath

docs.title: Everyone
docs.text: Name Title Where Role Marrun Keeper of the Oath Oath Hall Ruler Brask Captain of the Deep Watch Deep Watch Guard Thera Warden of the Seal Deep Watch Guard Oswin Master of the Ledgers Archive Scholar Kell Apprentice Archivist Archive Scholar Halvara Head of the Root Gardens Root Gardens Worker Corvan Keeper of the Stores Upper Stair Merchant Ysra Healer of the Halls Oath Hall Healer Gorran Smith of Cavelor Upper Stair Craftsman Doran Warden Back from the Surface Upper Stair Adventurer Varn Scout of the Outer Tunnels Deep Watch Adventurer Annick Singer of the Oath Oath Hall Performer Grisel Retired Warden Upper Stair Resident Ottel Child of the Root Gardens Root Gardens Child Rhenna Child of the Oath Hall Oath Hall Child

docs.title: Marrun
docs.text:
Keeper of the Oath

Role: Ruler · Age: Elder

Grave, patient and slow to speak, but his rare laughs fill the whole hall. He listens to everyone, from the oldest Warden to the smallest child, before he decides anything.

Marrun leads Cavelor and the Wardens of the Seal, and has walked the Deep Watch himself for longer than most of his people have been alive. For fifty years he has watched the seal weaken in the ledgers, and he spends more and more of his days writing to the surface, trying to make the kingdom understand how worried Cavelor is.

Relationships:

  • Brask: captain of the watch
  • Oswin: oldest friend
  • Grisel: former watch partner
  • Doran: trusted young messenger
  • Aveline: sworn ally

docs.title: Ysra
docs.text:
Healer of the Halls

Role: Healer · Age: Adult

Calm, gentle and immovable once she has made up her mind. She hums old Oath songs while she works.

Ysra tends to Wardens coming off the Deep Watch with scrapes, burns and the bone-weariness of long shifts. More of them come to her than they used to, and she worries that the watch is wearing her people down faster than they will admit.

Relationships:

  • Rhenna: daughter
  • Brask: patient who ignores her

docs.title: Annick
docs.text:
Singer of the Oath

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Lively, teasing and generous with her voice. She can turn the gloomiest Warden's shift change into a sing-along.

Annick keeps the old songs of the first guardians and teaches them to every child in Cavelor. Since Doran's return she has been trying to write a new song about the sun, and none of her verses feel right yet.

Relationships:

  • Corvan: sweetheart
  • Rhenna: pupil
  • Doran: source of sun stories

docs.title: Rhenna
docs.text:
Child of the Oath Hall

Role: Child · Age: Child

Shy, thoughtful and serious beyond her years. She already knows the whole Oath by heart.

Rhenna has never been to the surface and is a little afraid of an endless sky with no roof. She practises standing very straight so she will be ready to take her first turn as a Warden when she is grown.

Relationships:

  • Ysra: mother
  • Annick: teacher
  • Ottel: playmate

docs.title: Brask
docs.text:
Captain of the Deep Watch

Role: Guard · Age: Adult

Blunt, steady and tireless, with no patience for excuses and endless patience for a frightened recruit. Counts everything twice.

Brask draws up the turns of the Deep Watch, so that every adult in Cavelor takes a shift and no passage is ever left unwalked. Lately he has doubled the Wardens on the lowest passages, and he will not say aloud what he hears down there on quiet nights.

Relationships:

  • Marrun: keeper
  • Halvara: wife
  • Ottel: son
  • Thera: most dependable Warden
  • Gorran: friend
  • Varn: scout
  • Ysra: healer who scolds him

docs.title: Thera
docs.text:
Warden of the Seal

Role: Guard · Age: Young

Quiet, sharp-eyed and fiercely proud of her duty. She takes the Oath more seriously than anyone her age, and hates to be told to rest.

Thera stands the deepest watch she is allowed and reports every flicker in the seal's glow to the Archive, even the ones that turn out to be nothing. She has begun keeping a private notebook of small changes no one else has noticed, and she is not yet sure whom to show it.

Relationships:

  • Brask: captain
  • Gorran: father
  • Doran: brother
  • Oswin: archivist who reads her reports

docs.title: Varn
docs.text:
Scout of the Outer Tunnels

Role: Adventurer · Age: Adult

Wiry, wry and hard to rattle, with a scout's habit of standing with his back to the wall. Speaks in short sentences.

Varn maps the outer tunnels between Cavelor and the surface, where wild creatures have grown bold and vicious since the seal weakened. He has found tracks in passages that were empty for centuries and is looking for someone brave enough to help him follow them.

Relationships:

  • Brask: commander
  • Doran: rival

docs.title: Halvara
docs.text:
Head of the Root Gardens

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Warm, practical and always a little muddy. She talks to her mushrooms and feeds anyone who looks tired.

Halvara tends the pale mushroom beds and the root-fruit vines that keep all of Cavelor fed. Some of the deepest beds have been growing strangely these last few years, and she has asked the Archive to note it down, just in case it matters.

Relationships:

  • Brask: husband
  • Ottel: son
  • Corvan: buyer

docs.title: Ottel
docs.text:
Child of the Root Gardens

Role: Child · Age: Child

Curious, stubborn and fearless in the way of children who have never been told no for long. Collects interesting stones.

Ottel has never seen the sun and refuses to believe it is really as big as Doran says. He is saving his best stone to give to it.

Relationships:

  • Brask: father
  • Halvara: mother
  • Rhenna: playmate
  • Doran: storyteller

docs.title: Oswin
docs.text:
Master of the Ledgers

Role: Scholar · Age: Elder

Precise, dry and secretly sentimental. He can find any tremor in centuries of ledgers, but never his own spectacles.

Oswin keeps the great ledgers that go back to the founding, where every tremor and every change in the seal's glow is written down. He knows the page where the record changed fifty years ago by heart, and he has filled more ledgers since then than in all the years before.

Relationships:

  • Marrun: oldest friend
  • Kell: grandson
  • Thera: Warden who reports to him

docs.title: Kell
docs.text:
Apprentice Archivist

Role: Scholar · Age: Young

Eager, talkative and full of questions, with ink on every finger. He thinks out loud and apologises for it constantly.

Kell copies the old ledgers so that no record can be lost to damp or fire, and he loves the four peoples' stories about the Balrog that are tucked into their margins. He wishes someone would finally tell him which of the stories is true, and is beginning to suspect nobody knows.

Relationships:

  • Oswin: grandfather
  • Doran: best friend
  • Grisel: storyteller

docs.title: Corvan
docs.text:
Keeper of the Stores

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Dried mushrooms, root-fruit, lamp oil and lantern glass

Cheerful, chatty and a born haggler, though in Cavelor he mostly haggles for fun. Remembers what every family likes.

Corvan runs the stores at the top of the Upper Stair, where goods from the surface now arrive in small, precious loads. He has developed a great love of surface honey and keeps a jar hidden for special occasions.

Relationships:

  • Halvara: supplier
  • Annick: sweetheart

docs.title: Gorran
docs.text:
Smith of Cavelor

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder

Gruff, loud and soft-hearted, with a laugh like a hammer on stone. Believes any problem can be fixed if you heat it enough.

Gorran forges the Wardens' blades, lanterns and armour in his forge by the Upper Stair, where the old vents carry the smoke up through the rock. He has been asked to make more weapons each year since the monsters reached the outer tunnels, and he does not like what that means.

Relationships:

  • Brask: friend
  • Thera: daughter
  • Doran: son

docs.title: Doran
docs.text:
Warden Back from the Surface

Role: Adventurer · Age: Young

Bright, restless and impossible to keep quiet about the sky. He squints at every lantern now and calls it "almost as good as noon".

Doran went up with one of Marrun's messengers last year and saw the sun, the sea of grass and the towns of the surface for the first time. He loves all of it, and he feels guilty about how much he wants to go back while the seal grows weaker below.

Relationships:

  • Marrun: keeper who sent him to the surface
  • Gorran: father
  • Thera: sister
  • Kell: best friend
  • Annick: songwriter
  • Ottel: doubter
  • Varn: rival

docs.title: Grisel
docs.text:
Retired Warden

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Sharp-tongued, nosy and wickedly funny, with a memory for every scandal in Cavelor. Still sits facing the deep passages out of habit.

Grisel walked the Deep Watch for sixty years and was on shift the night the expedition first came down the stair. She tells the story to anyone who will listen, but always stops before the part where the seal changed.

Relationships:

  • Marrun: former watch partner
  • Kell: listener

docs.title: People of Fairy Forest
docs.text: The 35 people of Fairy Forest in the game's first release.

docs.title: Leaders
docs.text: • Calyra, Eldest of the Grove

docs.title: Calyra
docs.text:
Eldest of the Grove

Role: Ruler · Age: Elder

Patient and dry-humoured, she lets everyone finish speaking before she answers, and her answers are short. She still corrects students' spellwork out of habit.

Calyra taught at the Grove School for forty years before the forest's teachers and elders chose her from among themselves to be Eldest, and she now leads the Grove Council from the Heart Tree. Her quiet worry is the seal scholars, who sleep too little and find too little. An old friend among the Brenna of Midbarium still visits her each spring.

Relationships:

  • Thessaly: old rival and friend
  • Ilwen: steward
  • Amaryl: former student
  • Isaura: confidante
  • Halcy: friend
  • Odda: old friend

docs.title: Thessaly
docs.text:
Grove Councillor

Role: Council · Age: Elder

Proud, precise and quick to object, but the first to admit when she has been out-argued. She keeps a ledger of every promise the Council makes.

Thessaly was the other name spoken most often when the elders chose their Eldest, and she lost to Calyra by a handful of voices. She took it graciously and has been Calyra's sharpest critic and most reliable ally ever since.

Relationships:

  • Calyra: old rival and friend
  • Briony: sister

docs.title: Ilwen
docs.text:
Steward of the Heart Tree

Role: Official · Age: Adult

Calm, tidy and endlessly polite, with a habit of answering questions with the exact page and shelf where the answer can be found.

Ilwen keeps the Council's records, its meeting days and its guest list, and greets every visitor who climbs the Heart Tree's stair. He would like, just once, to take a holiday, but cannot think who would water the Council chamber's vines.

Relationships:

  • Calyra: employer
  • Wynne: friend

docs.title: Isaura
docs.text:
Keeper of the Old Records

Role: Scholar · Age: Elder

Stern, careful and secretive by duty rather than nature. She is gentler with her granddaughter than with anyone else.

Isaura guards the oldest Magician records, including what little remains about how the great seal was made, and leads the scholars studying it. Fifty years of reading have taught her a great deal about the seal and nothing yet about how to strengthen it. She has begun to suspect that some of the oldest pages were never written down at all.

Relationships:

  • Calyra: confidante
  • Caelum: student
  • Wynne: granddaughter

docs.title: Caelum
docs.text:
Seal Scholar

Role: Scholar · Age: Adult

Brilliant, restless and short on sleep, he talks quickly and forgets to eat. He hates admitting he is stuck.

Caelum has spent his whole working life comparing the old records with reports of how the monsters are changing, hoping the pattern will point to the seal's weak places. Every theory he has built so far has fallen apart, and he keeps a drawer of them labelled "wrong".

Relationships:

  • Isaura: mentor
  • Wynne: rival
  • Juniper: colleague

docs.title: Wynne
docs.text:
Copyist of the Old Records

Role: Scholar · Age: Young

Quiet, observant and stubborn. She notices what others skip and says so only when she is sure.

Wynne copies crumbling records onto fresh paper so the originals can rest. While copying she found a gap in the numbering of one old seal record, as though several pages were removed long ago, and she has not yet decided whom to tell.

Relationships:

  • Ilwen: friend
  • Isaura: grandmother
  • Caelum: rival

docs.title: Oriel
docs.text:
Master Treewright

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder

Gruff, gentle-handed and slow to trust anything that grew in less than a century.

Oriel tends the oldest living-tree homes around the Heart Tree, some of which the first Magicians coaxed from the trunks. Lately a few of the oldest homes have been slow to wake in spring, and he wants to know why before anyone else notices.

Relationships:

  • Aspen: old friend
  • Linnet: apprentice
  • Niv: friend

docs.title: Sorrel
docs.text:
Teacher of Listening

Role: Scholar · Age: Adult

Soft-spoken and unhurried, he believes most mistakes come from talking too much. His lessons are mostly silence, and his students love him anyway.

Sorrel teaches the first and oldest Magician lesson, how to listen to trees, wind and creatures before trying any magic at all. Lately he says the forest sounds uneasy at its edges, and he cannot explain what he means.

Relationships:

  • Aurel: student
  • Liri: student
  • Amaryl: colleague

docs.title: Amaryl
docs.text:
Teacher of Growing

Role: Scholar · Age: Elder

Brisk, warm and demanding, with no patience for shortcuts. She praises rarely and means it every time.

Amaryl teaches the coaxing of living wood, the craft behind the forest's tree homes. She was once Calyra's student, and still sometimes calls her "teacher" in Council by mistake.

Relationships:

  • Calyra: former teacher
  • Sorrel: colleague
  • Siora: student

docs.title: Aurel
docs.text:
Junior Teacher

Role: Scholar · Age: Young

Eager, nervous and over-prepared, he writes out every lesson word for word and then forgets the notes.

Aurel finished his own schooling only three years ago and now teaches the youngest students. He wants badly to prove he belongs at the front of the room.

Relationships:

  • Sorrel: mentor
  • Galen: brother

docs.title: Galen
docs.text:
Staff and Wand Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Staves, wands, spell scrolls and practice robes

Cheerful, talkative and a born salesman who never sells a student something too strong for them, however much they beg.

Galen keeps the little shop at the foot of the school stair and fits every new student with a first staff. He worries about his younger brother Aurel, and drops by his classroom far more often than he needs to.

Relationships:

  • Aurel: brother

docs.title: Liri
docs.text:
Grove School Student

Role: Child · Age: Child

Bright, bold and impatient, she wants to learn the exciting spells first and the listening never.

Liri was born in the forest and has been at the Grove School for one year. She has a plan to sneak out to the Forest Edge and see a real monster, and has told only her best friend.

Relationships:

  • Sorrel: teacher
  • Lumi: best friend
  • Tansy: mother

docs.title: Siora
docs.text:
Grove School Student

Role: Child · Age: Child

Shy, thoughtful and hard on herself, she practises long after everyone else has gone home.

Siora's gift is real but slow to wake, and her spells fizzle more often than they work. She is afraid of being sent home before it does.

Relationships:

  • Amaryl: teacher
  • Alder: friend

docs.title: Alder
docs.text:
Grove School Student

Role: Resident · Age: Young

Easygoing and funny, he hides his homesickness behind jokes about the forest having no sea.

Alder came from a harbour town to study at the Grove School, which teaches anyone with the gift. The road here was more dangerous than he expected, and he dreads the journey home at the end of term.

Relationships:

  • Siora: friend
  • Kestrel: hero

docs.title: Ondine
docs.text:
Keeper of the Lanterns

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder

Exacting, proud and secretly sentimental. She can tell which of her lanterns is dimming from across the forest.

Ondine leads the lantern-makers who light every path, bridge and stair in the forest. She has made the lanterns along the outer paths brighter each year as the woods beyond grow less friendly, and does not like what that says.

Relationships:

  • Faelan: apprentice
  • Vesper: daughter

docs.title: Faelan
docs.text:
Lantern-maker's Apprentice

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Dreamy and clumsy with his hands, but with a real eye for colour. He hums while he works.

Faelan has broken more lantern glass than any apprentice Ondine has ever taken. He is saving up to make a lantern of his own design as a gift for Linnet.

Relationships:

  • Ondine: mentor
  • Linnet: sweetheart

docs.title: Vesper
docs.text:
Lantern Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Lanterns, glow-oil and travelling lights

Sharp, practical and quick with a bargain, she has none of her mother's patience and all of her skill.

Vesper sells her mother's lanterns and her own, and her travelling lights have become popular with anyone who must use the roads after dark. She and Ondine argue about the shop's prices every single day.

Relationships:

  • Ondine: mother
  • Tansy: friend

docs.title: Tansy
docs.text:
Keeper of the Dewdrop Tea House

Role: Service · Age: Adult · Sells: Dew tea, honey cakes and a bed for the night

Warm, busy and impossible to surprise, she remembers every guest's favourite cake.

Tansy runs the tea house where students, travellers and scholars all end up sooner or later. She is raising her daughter Liri alone and suspects the girl is planning something.

Relationships:

  • Liri: daughter
  • Vesper: friend
  • Lyra: friend
  • Halcy: supplier

docs.title: Lyra
docs.text:
Singer of the Old Songs

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Bright, theatrical and generous, she will sing for anyone who asks and many who do not.

Lyra sings the forest's old songs on the Lantern Paths each evening, including the ones about the Balrog War. She learned most of them from her grandfather and is collecting the verses nobody else remembers.

Relationships:

  • Tansy: friend
  • Aspen: grandfather

docs.title: Aspen
docs.text:
Retired Treewright

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Talkative, nostalgic and stubborn about everything except his granddaughter.

Aspen was a young man when the expedition came back with news of the Children of the Tree, and he tells the story of that day to anyone who sits still long enough. He swears the forest was quieter before the Age of Disturbance, and he is probably right.

Relationships:

  • Lyra: granddaughter
  • Oriel: old friend
  • Sefa: friend

docs.title: Linnet
docs.text:
Keeper of Living Homes

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Patient, practical and a little too serious for her age. She talks to the trees she tends as if they were old neighbours.

Linnet keeps the living-tree homes along the Lantern Paths healthy, coaxing new rooms and mending storm damage. She is Oriel's apprentice and hopes one day to grow a home from a seedling herself.

Relationships:

  • Oriel: mentor
  • Faelan: sweetheart

docs.title: Lumi
docs.text:
Glade Dweller

Role: Resident · Age: Young · Kind: Child of the Tree

Endlessly curious and happily blunt, Lumi asks questions nobody else dares and laughs at most of the answers.

Lumi joined the Grove School to learn the forest's ways and has become Liri's best friend. Lumi knows about Liri's plan to visit the Forest Edge and is torn between keeping the secret and telling Tansy.

Relationships:

  • Liri: best friend
  • Sefa: friend

docs.title: Sefa
docs.text:
Glade Storyteller

Role: Performer · Age: Adult · Kind: Child of the Tree

Warm, playful and a natural entertainer, Sefa loves an audience and loves listening even more.

Sefa trades stories with the forest's children in the glade every afternoon, and with Aspen over tea. Sefa is gathering the forest's tales into one great collection, and refuses to say which stories are Sefa's own.

Relationships:

  • Aspen: friend
  • Lumi: friend

docs.title: Niv
docs.text:
Glade Dweller

Role: Resident · Age: Young · Kind: Child of the Tree

Shy, gentle and easily overwhelmed by crowds, Niv is fiercely loyal to the few people Niv trusts.

Niv lives in a tree home Oriel tended and visits him almost daily. Niv often stands at the edge of the glade looking toward the World Tree and has never told anyone why.

Relationships:

  • Oriel: friend
  • Halcy: guide

docs.title: Orla
docs.text:
Glade Dweller

Role: Resident · Age: Young · Kind: Child of the Tree

Mischievous, quick-witted and never cruel, Orla thinks the forest takes itself far too seriously.

Orla is the one playing tricks on Thorne at night, mostly moving his things a little to the left. Orla has decided Thorne needs to laugh more and will not stop until he does.

Relationships:

  • Thorne: target

docs.title: Halcy
docs.text:
Garland Weaver

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Kind: Child of the Tree · Sells: Woven baskets and glade-flower garlands

Kind, practical and welcoming, Halcy remembers everyone's name after one meeting.

Halcy was among the first of the Children to settle in Fairy Forest and helps newer arrivals find their way. Calyra counts Halcy as a friend and sometimes asks for advice over a basket of flowers.

Relationships:

  • Calyra: friend
  • Tansy: customer
  • Niv: friend

docs.title: Hesper
docs.text:
Mistress of the Herb Gardens

Role: Healer · Age: Elder

Blunt, kind and always smelling faintly of mint. She treats grown adults exactly the way she treats children with scraped knees.

Hesper has tended the forest's healing gardens for most of her life and taught half its herbalists. More hurt travellers come to her each year from the roads, and she has started keeping a list of what attacked them.

Relationships:

  • Celandine: apprentice
  • Merrow: gardener
  • Briony: friend

docs.title: Celandine
docs.text:
Herbalist

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Healing salves, herb teas and potions

Gentle, orderly and a little anxious, she labels everything twice.

Celandine runs the remedy stall by the garden gate and makes most of what she sells. She wants to find a plant that grows only near the Forest Edge, but her husband begs her not to go.

Relationships:

  • Hesper: mentor
  • Merrow: husband

docs.title: Merrow
docs.text:
Gardener

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Big-hearted, slow-talking and fiercely protective of his beds of seedlings.

Merrow does the digging, weeding and watering that keeps the gardens alive. He is proud of his wife's remedies and quietly afraid of the Forest Edge, where she keeps wanting to go.

Relationships:

  • Hesper: employer
  • Celandine: wife
  • Ailo: friend

docs.title: Briony
docs.text:
Grove Councillor

Role: Council · Age: Elder

Merry, gossipy and wiser than she lets on. She prefers to settle disagreements over tea rather than in the Council chamber.

Briony taught herb-lore at the Grove School for decades and still spends more time in the gardens than at the Heart Tree. She is Thessaly's younger sister, and the only person who can make her laugh during a Council meeting.

Relationships:

  • Thessaly: sister
  • Hesper: friend

docs.title: Ailo
docs.text:
Garden Helper

Role: Worker · Age: Adult · Kind: Child of the Tree

Calm, unhurried and deeply content, Ailo can work for hours without a word and seems to enjoy every minute.

Ailo helps in the Herb Gardens and has become close friends with Merrow. Hesper says the gardens have never grown so well, and Ailo only smiles when asked why.

Relationships:

  • Merrow: friend

docs.title: Seren
docs.text:
Warden of the Forest Edge

Role: Guard · Age: Adult

Steady, watchful and few-worded, she would rather turn a visitor back politely than draw a weapon.

Seren commands the small watch at the forest's edge, which once only stopped visitors from taking more than the forest could spare. Now it also keeps monsters from the paths, and she has asked the Council more than once for more hands.

Relationships:

  • Thorne: guard
  • Kestrel: friend
  • Juniper: friend

docs.title: Thorne
docs.text:
Edge Guard

Role: Guard · Age: Young

Brash, brave and much too eager for a fight. He is a better guard than he looks and a worse one than he thinks.

Thorne joined the edge watch to see some action and has seen plenty. He is convinced someone in the forest is playing tricks on him at night, and he is right.

Relationships:

  • Seren: captain
  • Kestrel: rival
  • Orla: secret prankster

docs.title: Kestrel
docs.text:
Wandering Magician

Role: Adventurer · Age: Young

Restless, cocky and loyal, she treats every monster on the road as a personal insult.

Kestrel finished at the Grove School and went straight out onto the roads, clearing monsters from the paths between towns. She stops at the Forest Edge between journeys to trade news with the watch and tease Thorne.

Relationships:

  • Alder: admirer
  • Seren: friend
  • Thorne: rival

docs.title: Juniper
docs.text:
Wilds Naturalist

Role: Adventurer · Age: Adult

Curious, fearless and careless about her own safety, she sketches creatures while they are still trying to bite her.

Juniper travels the wilds recording how creatures have changed during the Age of Disturbance, and brings her notes back for the seal scholars. Her notebooks are full, but nobody has yet found what the changes mean.

Relationships:

  • Caelum: colleague
  • Seren: friend

docs.title: People of Goa Harbour
docs.text: The 45 people of Goa Harbour in the game's first release.

docs.title: Leaders
docs.text: • Iska, First Warden
