docs.title: Rook
docs.text:
Caller of the Open Table

Role: Ruler · Age: Adult

Dry, patient and quick to laugh, with a voice that can cut through a shouting hall without ever sounding angry. Rook hates making speeches and loves listening to them.

The Open Table chose Rook as this year's Caller, which means convening the Table, keeping order and making sure the quiet ones get a turn; it does not mean ruling anyone, and Rook reminds people of that often. Rook keeps up a long, warm exchange of letters with the capital and reads the funniest parts aloud at the Table.

Relationships:

  • Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash: colleague at the Table
  • Bastian 'Bellows' Krell: favorite heckler
  • Quint: old friend and adviser
  • Mags: friend
  • Saucer: tea seller
  • Nana Gristle: scolding elder
  • Brindle: captain who reports to the Table
  • Aveline: frequent correspondent

docs.title: Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash
docs.text:
Scribe of the Open Table

Role: Official · Age: Adult

Precise, ink-stained and secretly delighted by every argument. She writes down the jokes as carefully as the decisions.

Dimity has kept the Table's record for twelve years, and her shelves hold every heckle and every vote. She is quietly worried that the oldest record books, from the first winters, are crumbling and nobody has copied them.

Relationships:

  • Rook: colleague at the Table
  • Ozzie Lantry: fellow keeper of records

docs.title: Quint
docs.text:
Keeper of the Charter Scroll

Role: Official · Age: Elder

Solemn about exactly one thing, the Open Charter, and cheerfully unserious about everything else.

Quint guards the hall's copy of the Open Charter ruling and reads it aloud every Walkout Day morning before the play. He likes to remind young hotheads that the kingdom chose to welcome the Walkers, and that this is worth being proud of.

Relationships:

  • Rook: friend
  • Ozzie Lantry: old friend
  • Dina Finch: director

docs.title: Bastian 'Bellows' Krell
docs.text:
Loudest Voice at the Table

Role: Council · Age: Adult

Enormous voice, enormous opinions, enormous heart. He changes his mind loudly and without shame.

Bastian has spoken at every Open Table for twenty years and has never once been short. This year he is campaigning, at length, for a covered bridge over Lantern Square so the night market can run in the rain.

Relationships:

  • Rook: patient listener
  • Mags: wife

docs.title: Mags
docs.text:
Cook of the Great Hall

Role: Service · Age: Adult

Brisk and bossy in the kitchen, soft as bread dough everywhere else. She judges people by whether they wash their own bowl.

Mags feeds the Open Table, which can run until dawn, from one huge pot of stew that she claims has never been fully emptied since her grandmother's day. She would like someone to invent a stove that does not smoke.

Relationships:

  • Rook: grateful regular
  • Bastian 'Bellows' Krell: husband
  • Old Parsnip: vegetable supplier

docs.title: Ozzie Lantry
docs.text:
Historian of the Walkers

Role: Scholar · Age: Elder

Gentle, rambling and easily sidetracked by a good anecdote. He keeps three pairs of spectacles and can never find any of them.

Ozzie collects letters, diaries and songs from the Walkers and their children, and is writing a history of Urbanograd's first hundred years. He is missing every account of the first winter and would pay well for anyone who finds one in an old attic.

Relationships:

  • Dimity 'Inkpot' Ash: fellow keeper of records
  • Quint: old friend
  • Wendel 'Dog-Ear' Tuck: teasing bookseller

docs.title: Lux
docs.text:
Keeper of the Lanterns

Role: Official · Age: Adult

Calm, watchful and fond of heights. Lux speaks softly and notices every lantern that has gone out.

Lux climbs the towers every dusk to relight the lanterns strung between them, a job that has passed through a dozen hands since the Walkers hung the first ones. Lately some of the lanterns facing the wilds have been found smashed in the mornings, and Lux would like to know by what.

Relationships:

  • Tinsel: glass supplier
  • Perch: friend
  • Prism: friend

docs.title: Jinx
docs.text:
Juggler of Lantern Square

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Restless, cheeky and terrible at keeping secrets. Jinx drops things on purpose to make children laugh, and almost never by accident.

Jinx juggles anything handed over, from apples to Margo's spare parts, and passes the hat afterwards. The dream is to juggle burning torches on top of the theatre cart on Walkout Day, which the troupe has firmly refused so far.

Relationships:

  • Drum: street partner
  • Figgy: favorite juggler
  • Tinder: friend

docs.title: Drum
docs.text:
Bucket Drummer

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Says almost nothing and lets the rhythm talk. Drum smiles only when someone in the crowd starts dancing.

Drum plays a ring of upturned buckets and pans every evening, and the night market sets its pace by the beat. Drum is trying to work out a rhythm loud enough to keep monsters away from the roads, half as a joke and half not.

Relationships:

  • Jinx: street partner
  • Saffi: bandmate

docs.title: Saffi
docs.text:
Fiddler of Lantern Square

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Fierce, fast and impatient with anything slow, including her own fingers. She laughs at her own mistakes before anyone else can.

Saffi came from a family of respectable musicians who wanted her to play slow court dances, so she plays everything twice as fast. She is writing a tune for every street in the city and has finished nine.

Relationships:

  • Piper: admirer
  • Drum: bandmate

docs.title: Ochre
docs.text:
Muralist

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult

Big-hearted and messy, always speckled with paint. Ochre talks to walls as if they were old friends.

Ochre has painted half the walls around the square and repaints the oldest ones every spring so the Walkers' first pictures never fade. Ochre wants to paint the whole history of the city along the Gate Walk but cannot get enough red paint.

Relationships:

  • Figgy: daughter
  • Splash: rival painter

docs.title: Figgy
docs.text:
Chalk Artist

Role: Child · Age: Child

Bright, bossy and stubborn, with chalk dust up to the elbows. Figgy insists every drawing is finished only when it rains.

Ochre's daughter draws on every flagstone in the square and charges passers-by one copper to step on her pictures. She wants a real wall of her own.

Relationships:

  • Jinx: favorite audience
  • Ochre: mother

docs.title: Nana Gristle
docs.text:
Bench-Sitter of Lantern Square

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Sharp-tongued, sweet-toothed and impossible to shock. She knows everyone's grandparents and all their embarrassing stories.

Nana Gristle's mother was carried out of Selsior in a basket on the day of the Long Walk, and Nana treats this as the city's most important fact. She sits on the same bench every day and tells newcomers which rooftops to avoid.

Relationships:

  • Rook: fond listener
  • Saucer: old friend

docs.title: Ivo Sable
docs.text:
Street Healer

Role: Healer · Age: Adult

Unhurried, gentle and very hard to rattle. He talks to patients about music to take their minds off the stitches.

Ivo runs a little clinic under an awning on the square, mostly patching up rooftop tumbles and burnt fingers. More and more of his patients are travelers hurt on the roads, and he is running short of the bandages and salves that come in from outside.

Relationships:

  • Crow: stubborn colleague
  • Patch: fellow healer
  • Tinder: frequent patient

docs.title: Tinder
docs.text:
Fire-Eater

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Swaggering and showy on stage, careful and nervous off it. Tinder checks the water bucket three times before every show.

Tinder learned to eat fire from a traveling show and settled here because nobody told her to stop. She refuses to perform anywhere near the old stories of the Burning, which she says are bad luck.

Relationships:

  • Jinx: friend
  • Ivo Sable: healer

docs.title: Margo 'Sparks' Venn
docs.text:
Inventor of Sparking Things

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult · Sells: Gadgets, spring-traps and sparking lamps

Brilliant, scatterbrained and slightly singed. Margo explains every invention three ways before she lets anyone touch it.

Margo's workshop is the one with the smoke stains around the door. She is building a lamp that throws sparks to frighten off road monsters, and needs someone brave enough to test it outside the walls.

Relationships:

  • Bolt: apprentice
  • Rivet: rival
  • Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway: gadget tester

docs.title: Cobble
docs.text:
Bootmaker

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder · Sells: Boots, rooftop slippers and repairs

Grumpy, honest and proud. Cobble says a boot should outlive its owner and means it.

Cobble makes the soft-soled boots that rooftop runners swear by, and has made them for three generations of Kites. He wants an apprentice but has rejected every one so far for having the wrong sort of hands.

Relationships:

  • Kite: loyal customer
  • Edgar Penhallow: would-be apprentice

docs.title: Hex
docs.text:
Puzzle-Box Maker

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult · Sells: Puzzle boxes, locks and clever latches

Sly, playful and secretive. Hex answers every question with a riddle unless you are buying something.

Hex builds boxes that open only for the right sequence of taps and turns. One of Hex's earliest boxes was sold years ago and has come back unopened with a note saying the buyer could not solve it, and Hex cannot remember the trick either.

Relationships:

  • Velvet: friend

docs.title: Bolt
docs.text:
Tinker's Apprentice

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Eager, clumsy and full of ideas that almost work. Bolt apologizes to every machine he breaks.

Bolt is Margo's apprentice and does most of the sweeping and all of the testing. He secretly thinks some of Rivet's ideas are better than Margo's and is afraid to say so.

Relationships:

  • Margo 'Sparks' Venn: mentor

docs.title: Tinsel
docs.text:
Glassblower

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult · Sells: Lantern glass, bottles and glass beads

Dreamy, slow-spoken and fascinated by light. Tinsel holds every bit of glass up to the sun before selling it.

Tinsel makes the colored lantern glass that gives Urbanograd its glow at night. Tinsel is trying to make a glass that glows on its own and so far has only made some very pretty paperweights.

Relationships:

  • Lux: customer
  • Starling: friend

docs.title: Ferro
docs.text:
Smith of Odd Metals

Role: Craftsman · Age: Adult · Sells: Daggers, throwing stars, claws and knuckle guards

Gruff, exacting and secretly sentimental. Ferro names every blade before it leaves the forge.

Ferro used to make only metal sculptures, but with the roads getting worse the adventurers keep asking for weapons, so now Ferro makes those too and grumbles about it. Ferro still welds a sculpture every Walkout Day and gives it away.

Relationships:

  • Shade: customer
  • Hatch: old customer

docs.title: Dyna
docs.text:
Tailor of Loud Clothes

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Patchwork coats, bright scarves and stage clothes

Flamboyant, frank and generous with compliments. Dyna thinks beige is a moral failing.

Dyna dyes cloth in colors no guild would allow and sells clothes stitched from a dozen fabrics at once. Visitors from the capital buy her coats to wear at home, which she finds very funny.

Relationships:

  • Thimble: haggling customer

docs.title: Rivet
docs.text:
Builder of the Rooftop Lift

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Cocky, competitive and very practical. Rivet would rather build something that works than something that sparkles.

Rivet built the rope-and-pulley lift that hauls crates up to the Rooftops and wants to build a second one, if the Open Table agrees. Rivet and Margo argue about everything and would both be lost without each other.

Relationships:

  • Margo 'Sparks' Venn: rival
  • Edgar Penhallow: admirer
  • Vane: partner on rooftop projects

docs.title: Edgar Penhallow
docs.text:
Guild Apprentice from Selsior

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Polite, earnest and slowly loosening up. Edgar still says please to doors.

Edgar's guild in Selsior sent him to study Urbanograd's workshops for a season, and he has filled four notebooks. He is beginning to suspect he does not want to go back, and has not written home about it.

Relationships:

  • Rivet: friend
  • Cobble: unimpressed teacher

docs.title: Moth
docs.text:
Keeper of the Night Market Stalls

Role: Official · Age: Adult

Wry, tireless and allergic to mornings. Moth knows which stall is where by smell alone.

Moth assigns the stalls each evening by drawing names from a hat, the way the first traders did, so no one owns the best corner for long. Moth has noticed fewer traders arriving from outside since the roads turned dangerous and worries about the winter.

Relationships:

  • Glim: daughter
  • Hester 'Ladle' Cray: friend

docs.title: Hester 'Ladle' Cray
docs.text:
Skewer Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Grilled skewers, pepper buns and hot cider

Loud, cheerful and always waving a ladle as if conducting a choir. She remembers every regular's order.

Ladle's stall is the first one lit and the last one dark. She is quietly feeding a few rooftop children for free and pretends not to know it.

Relationships:

  • Moth: friend
  • Scrap: grateful friend
  • Remy Marlo: stall neighbour

docs.title: Velvet
docs.text:
Trader of Curios

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Curios, trinkets and oddities from across Veligor

Silky, mysterious and a little theatrical. Velvet tells a story with every sale, and some of the stories are true.

Velvet buys odd things from travelers and sells them at a mark-up to anyone charmed enough. Among her stock is a dark stone that stays warm to the touch, bought from a frightened wanderer off the deep roads, and she will not say what she thinks it is.

Relationships:

  • Hex: friend
  • Nix: friend

docs.title: Crow
docs.text:
Tonic Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Healing tonics, mana draughts and remedies

Deadpan, sharp and suspicious of anyone who haggles too sweetly. Crow wears black because it hides spills.

Crow brews tonics in the back of the stall and sells them by lantern light. Ivo keeps telling Crow to label the bottles properly, and Crow keeps ignoring him.

Relationships:

  • Ivo Sable: exasperated colleague

docs.title: Nix
docs.text:
Mask Maker

Role: Merchant · Age: Young · Sells: Masks, face paint and Walkout Day costumes

Shy behind a counter, bold behind a mask. Nix speaks more easily in a voice that is not their own.

Nix makes the paper masks everyone wears on Walkout Day, and this year has been asked to make a new Juna mask for the play. Nix is terrified of getting her face wrong.

Relationships:

  • Velvet: friend
  • Pip Marrow: model

docs.title: Wendel 'Dog-Ear' Tuck
docs.text:
Seller of Old Books and Banned Plays

Role: Merchant · Age: Elder · Sells: Second-hand books, play scripts and song sheets

Cheerfully disorganized and fiercely well-read. He folds down page corners and calls it a public service.

Dog-Ear sells books that were once frowned on somewhere and are now simply old. He claims to own a script of Juna's play written in her own hand, and Ozzie has been trying to see it for ten years.

Relationships:

  • Ozzie Lantry: frustrated would-be buyer

docs.title: Glim
docs.text:
Paper Lantern Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Young · Sells: Paper lanterns and candle stubs

Cheerful, chatty and a born salesperson. Glim can sell a lantern to someone already holding two.

Moth's daughter runs her own little stall at the end of the market and is saving up to buy a cart. She wants to take her lanterns to other towns one day, if the roads ever get safer.

Relationships:

  • Moth: father
  • Saucer: adopted grandparent

docs.title: Remy Marlo
docs.text:
Smoked Fish Seller

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Smoked fish, sea-salt crisps and pickled kelp

Breezy, patient and homesick for the sound of waves. He hums sea songs when business is slow.

Remy came inland from the coast two years ago because he fell in love with the night market on a visit. The fish deliveries are getting harder to bring in safely, and he is wondering whether to learn a new trade.

Relationships:

  • Crumb: fellow newcomer
  • Hester 'Ladle' Cray: stall neighbour

docs.title: Saucer
docs.text:
Tea Stall Keeper

Role: Merchant · Age: Elder · Sells: Spiced tea, honey cakes and fortune leaves

Serene, mischievous and full of terrible puns. Saucer reads tea leaves and always predicts something nice.

Saucer has run the same tea stall for forty years and claims to have served tea to every Caller of the Open Table. Saucer is getting slow and hopes someone will take over the stall, but will not admit it.

Relationships:

  • Rook: regular customer
  • Nana Gristle: old friend
  • Glim: helper

docs.title: Crumb
docs.text:
Baker from the Farmlands

Role: Merchant · Age: Adult · Sells: Bread, rolls and sweet buns

Warm, sturdy and a little baffled by city life. Crumb still wakes at dawn even though he works all night.

Crumb grew up on a farm in the green country and came to Urbanograd to bake bread shaped like whatever he liked. His dragon-shaped loaves are a hit, and his family back home still thinks it is a phase.

Relationships:

  • Remy Marlo: fellow newcomer
  • Rue: friend from the farmlands

docs.title: Vane
docs.text:
Rooftop Bridge-Builder

Role: Worker · Age: Adult

Fearless, practical and calm in a high wind. Vane tests every plank by jumping on it.

Vane builds and mends the plank bridges between Urbanograd's rooftops, and knows every one by name. Vane is trying to raise Scrap well and worries about the day she wants to go out on the roads.

Relationships:

  • Scrap: daughter
  • Rivet: partner on rooftop projects

docs.title: Kite
docs.text:
Rooftop Runner

Role: Worker · Age: Young

Fast, boastful and impossible to keep on the ground. Kite talks while running and never runs out of breath.

Kite carries messages across the city by rooftop and holds the record for the run from the Gate Walk to the Great Hall. Kite's mother and grandmother were runners too and all wore Cobble's boots.

Relationships:

  • Cobble: bootmaker
  • Splash: sweetheart

docs.title: Perch
docs.text:
Pigeon Keeper

Role: Resident · Age: Elder

Soft-spoken, patient and covered in feathers. Perch understands birds better than people and admits it.

Perch keeps message pigeons in a loft on the highest roof in the city. Over the last few years the birds have begun refusing certain routes over the wilds, and Perch keeps a careful list of which ones.

Relationships:

  • Lux: friend
  • Pounce: uninvited lodger
  • Old Parsnip: rooftop neighbour
  • Starling: friend

docs.title: Scrap
docs.text:
Rooftop Scamp

Role: Child · Age: Child

Nimble, nosy and fearless in all the wrong places. Scrap collects lost things and gives them names.

Scrap is Vane's daughter and has never once used the stairs. She wants to be an adventurer like Shade and practices sneaking on everyone.

Relationships:

  • Hester 'Ladle' Cray: secret feeder
  • Vane: mother
  • Shade: hero

docs.title: Starling
docs.text:
Rooftop Stargazer

Role: Scholar · Age: Adult

Distracted, kind and wildly enthusiastic about anything in the sky. Starling sleeps through every afternoon.

Starling maps the stars from a telescope built out of Tinsel's spare lenses. On some nights the horizon toward the middle of the island seems to flicker, and Starling has started writing down the dates without knowing what they mean.

Relationships:

  • Tinsel: lens maker
  • Perch: friend

docs.title: Old Parsnip
docs.text:
Rooftop Gardener

Role: Worker · Age: Elder

Slow, earthy and stubbornly hopeful. Old Parsnip talks to seedlings and swears they listen.

Old Parsnip grows vegetables in tubs and troughs across the rooftops, a habit the city picked up after the Walkers nearly starved their first winter. With fewer food carts arriving, more people are asking him for seeds.

Relationships:

  • Perch: rooftop neighbour
  • Mags: customer

docs.title: Pounce
docs.text:
Rooftop Cat

Role: Animal · Age: Adult

Lazy by day, dignified by night and certain that every roof belongs to him.

Pounce is a big grey cat who sleeps in Perch's pigeon loft, which the pigeons have accepted with deep reluctance. Rooftop folk say he always knows when the weather is about to turn.

Relationships:

  • Perch: keeper
  • Rue: rehearsal partner

docs.title: Splash
docs.text:
Night Painter

Role: Craftsman · Age: Young

Restless, playful and allergic to permission. Splash never signs a painting and never stops grinning.

Splash paints murals on the backs of chimneys and the undersides of bridges overnight, where only rooftop folk can see them. Splash wants to paint something that can be seen from the Gate Walk, so travelers know they have arrived.

Relationships:

  • Ochre: rival painter
  • Kite: sweetheart

docs.title: Dina Finch
docs.text:
Director of the Old Barracks Troupe

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

Commanding, theatrical and warm under the bluster. Dina gives notes even at breakfast.

Dina runs the troupe that performs Juna Marrow's play on a cart every Walkout Day, as it was first performed. She is determined that this year's play will be the funniest in a decade, and she has said so every year for a decade.

Relationships:

  • Pip Marrow: protégée
  • Dex: lead actor
  • Piper: songwriter
  • Rue: lead actress
  • Quint: opening speaker

docs.title: Pip Marrow
docs.text:
Juna's Great-Granddaughter

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Witty, self-doubting and quick with a comeback. Pip hates being introduced by her surname.

Pip is descended from Juna Marrow, and everyone expects her to write a play as good as Juna's. She has written three and burned two, and she is secretly working on a new comedy she will not show anyone.

Relationships:

  • Dina Finch: mentor
  • Hambone: keeper of her ancestor's cart
  • Nix: mask maker

docs.title: Dex
docs.text:
Plays the Grandee

Role: Performer · Age: Adult

A born clown with a booming voice and an ego to match, but generous with every laugh he gets.

Dex has played the pompous grandee in Juna's play for fifteen years and knows every line of every part. He wants to try a serious role just once, and nobody will take him seriously.

Relationships:

  • Dina Finch: director
  • Sprout: son

docs.title: Rue
docs.text:
Plays Juna on Walkout Day

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Quiet, observant and stricken with stage fright until the very moment she steps on. Then she is fearless.

Rue came to the city from Kaldemor's farmlands three years ago and won the part of Juna this spring, to everyone's surprise including her own. She practices her lines on Pounce, who is not much help.

Relationships:

  • Crumb: friend from the farmlands
  • Dina Finch: director
  • Pounce: unimpressed audience

docs.title: Hambone
docs.text:
Keeper of the Theatre Cart

Role: Worker · Age: Elder

Sentimental, stubborn and a very bad liar. Hambone polishes the cart wheels while humming the play's songs.

Hambone looks after the old cart the troupe performs on every Walkout Day, and swears some of its planks come from Juna's own cart. One wheel is cracking, and he cannot bear to replace it.

Relationships:

  • Thimble: old friend
  • Pip Marrow: friend

docs.title: Thimble
docs.text:
Costume Maker

Role: Craftsman · Age: Elder

Fussy, sharp-eyed and secretly sentimental. Thimble has pins in her mouth at all times and still talks.

Thimble has sewn the troupe's costumes for thirty years and keeps the grandee's ridiculous hat locked away between shows. She buys her brightest fabric from Dyna and complains about the price every time.

Relationships:

  • Dyna: supplier
  • Hambone: old friend

docs.title: Piper
docs.text:
Songwriter of the Troupe

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Romantic, scatterbrained and always humming something new. Piper falls in love with a melody a week.

Piper writes new songs for the play every year, to Dina's despair and the crowd's delight. Piper wants to play with Saffi but is too shy to ask.

Relationships:

  • Saffi: admired musician
  • Dina Finch: exasperated director

docs.title: Sprout
docs.text:
Troupe Urchin

Role: Child · Age: Child

Giggly, loud and never still. Sprout has learned every part in the play by accident.

Dex's son plays the market urchin who cheers for Juna in the first scene, and he steals the show every year. He wants to play the grandee one day so he can wear the hat.

Relationships:

  • Dex: father

docs.title: Brindle
docs.text:
Captain of the Gate Watch

Role: Guard · Age: Adult

Steady, plain-spoken and dryly funny. Brindle believes in good boots, good lanterns and checking twice.

Brindle commands the small volunteer watch that guards the old fortress gate. Brindle has asked the Open Table for more volunteers this year, because monsters now come closer to the walls than they used to.

Relationships:

  • Knox: guard
  • Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe: guard
  • Rook: friend

docs.title: Knox
docs.text:
Gate Watch Guard

Role: Guard · Age: Adult

Big, gentle and slow to anger. Knox carves little wooden animals during quiet watches.

Knox has guarded the gate for ten years and knows every regular traveler by face. He would like his son Tick to choose a safer life and is losing that argument.

Relationships:

  • Brindle: captain
  • Tick: son

docs.title: Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe
docs.text:
Night Watch Guard

Role: Guard · Age: Young

Jumpy, sharp-eyed and talkative to fight off the dark. She carries two lamps because one went out once.

Dagny keeps the gate on the night watch and has seen eyes in the dark beyond the road more often this year than last. She is braver than she thinks and has not noticed yet.

Relationships:

  • Brindle: captain
  • Patch: healer

docs.title: Shade
docs.text:
Knife-Thrower and Road Guide

Role: Adventurer · Age: Adult

Cool, quiet and secretly soft on children. Shade never misses and never brags.

Shade guides travelers and traders safely along the roads into the city, for a fee and a hot meal. The routes Shade trusted a few years ago are not safe anymore, and Shade is looking for new ones.

Relationships:

  • Ferro: smith
  • Scrap: admirer
  • Hatch: old mentor

docs.title: Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway
docs.text:
Young Adventurer

Role: Adventurer · Age: Young

Reckless, sunny and determined to be famous. Zip has never met a dare she would refuse.

Zip grew up in the city and left on her first adventure last spring, coming back with a broken arm and a great story. She has volunteered to test Margo's spark lamp on real monsters.

Relationships:

  • Margo 'Sparks' Venn: inventor
  • Torvi Brask: teacher

docs.title: Hatch
docs.text:
Monster Hunter

Role: Adventurer · Age: Elder

Weathered, blunt and full of stories he tells only after the second cup. Hatch trusts his nose more than any map.

Hatch has hunted on Veligor's roads for thirty years and says the monsters today are nothing like the ones of his youth. He is too old to go out alone now and is looking for someone worth teaching.

Relationships:

  • Ferro: smith
  • Tick: admirer
  • Shade: former pupil

docs.title: Torvi Brask
docs.text:
Axe-Fighter from the Highlands

Role: Adventurer · Age: Adult

Proud, honest and bemused by city manners. Torvi laughs like a rockslide.

Torvi came down from the highlands to see the city everyone talks about and stayed because the music was good. Torvi hires out as a caravan guard and is teaching Zip to fight properly.

Relationships:

  • Zinnia 'Zip' Calloway: student

docs.title: Prism
docs.text:
Light-Painter from the Forest

Role: Performer · Age: Young

Curious, earnest and delighted by everything. Prism asks questions faster than anyone can answer them.

Prism grew up in the forest learning a little magic and came to Urbanograd to use it for art, painting pictures with small lights in the air for travelers arriving at the gate. Prism hopes to put on a light show for Walkout Day.

Relationships:

  • Lux: friend

docs.title: Patch
docs.text:
Herbalist of the Gate Walk

Role: Healer · Age: Elder

Brusque, practical and quietly tender. Patch scolds patients while bandaging them.

Patch tends the travelers who stumble in through the gate with monster bites and scrapes. Her herb supplies come from outside the walls, and she needs someone to gather fresh ones now that the fields are risky.

Relationships:

  • Ivo Sable: fellow healer
  • Dagny 'Two-Lamps' Roe: friend

docs.title: Tick
docs.text:
Gate Messenger

Role: Child · Age: Child

Eager, earnest and always out of breath. Tick salutes everyone, including the cat.

Knox's son runs messages from the gate to the rest of the city and dreams of being an adventurer like Hatch. He keeps a notebook of every traveler's strange story.

Relationships:

  • Knox: father
  • Hatch: reluctant hero

docs.title: Bain Harbour
docs.text:
The Coastal Town

Bain Harbour is a prosperous port on one coast of Veligor. It feels like a little of Selsior and a little of Kaldemor, with town life, cheerful craftsmanship and busy trade all meeting the sea.

docs.title: The Fishermen's Cove
docs.text: Bain Harbour began as a cove of Commons fishing families, who found that the deep, sheltered bay was the one place on that coast where boats could ride out a storm. Through the Age of Division, the cove stayed small and kept its head down, selling fish to whichever side came to buy and trying hard to stay out of the wars.

docs.title: The Shipwrights' Century
docs.text:
After the founding, peace changed everything. With the island united, goods needed to move from one end of Veligor to the other, and the sea was often the fastest road. The fishing families took up shipbuilding, and the cove's sheltered water became the island's busiest shipyard. Merchants followed the ships, craftsmen followed the merchants, and the cove grew into a town.

The town takes its name from Old Bain, a fisherwoman remembered as the first to build a ship big enough to sail around the island. Her boat-hook still hangs above the door of the harbour hall.

docs.title: A Town of Its Own
docs.text: As it grew, both Selsior and Kaldemor did a great deal of business through Bain Harbour, and more than once someone in the capital suggested that the port ought to answer to the crown's own officials. The people of Bain Harbour politely refused every time. The harbour is run by its own harbour council, made up of its captains, shipwrights and merchants, and the town is proud that no one else has ever had a say in its affairs.

docs.title: Environment and Identity
docs.text:
Bain Harbour is a town of docks and waterfront houses, markets and shipwrights' workshops, warehouses and lighthouses, and everything travellers and traders need. Its look and spirit blend city and countryside: Selsior's busy streets and stone, Kaldemor's colorful wood and cheer. It is welcoming, prosperous and always sociable, and it smells of tar, salt and fresh bread.

Since the Age of Disturbance began, the sea around Veligor has grown rougher and stranger, and Bain Harbour's sailors tell of creatures in the deep water that were never there before. The harbour's ships still sail, but its captains now hire adventurers to sail with them.

docs.title: Independence
docs.text:
Bain Harbour is not Selsior's port, nor Kaldemor's. It is a town in its own right, with its own history, people and identity. What it shares with those towns is a feeling, not a chain of command, and it belongs to Wonder Kingdom on equal terms with every other settlement.

It lies on the opposite side of the island from Goa Harbour. The two ports are very different, but they are friends, not rivals, and they hold a friendly boat race between them every summer that goes all the way around Veligor.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Bain Harbour.

Design notes

New with this page: the fishing cove origin, Old Bain, the harbour council, the summer race around Veligor, and sea creatures stirred up by the Disturbance. Still open: which coast Bain Harbour is on.

docs.title: Cavelor
docs.text:
The Underground City of Guardians

Cavelor is a small and very old city hidden deep beneath the World Tree. It was founded right after the first war against the Balrog, when some of the greatest warriors and guardians of that age chose to stay below and keep watch over the seal.

docs.title: The Oath Below
docs.text:
When the seal was finished and the four armies began to march home, a company of warriors stayed behind in the roots. They came from all four peoples: Savage warriors, Magicians who understood the seal, Commons who knew how to dig and build, and Aristocrat officers to lead them. They swore an oath, the Oath Below, to watch the Balrog's prison for as long as it held, and to send word to the surface if it ever began to fail.

Then they were nearly forgotten. The surface celebrated, the kingdom grew, and within a few generations, the guardians beneath the Tree had faded into legend. Kragvar songs in Midbarium still claimed that some of their warriors stayed below, but few took the songs as anything more than stories.

docs.title: A City in the Roots
docs.text:
Below, the guardians built a home. They carved halls out of the rock between the great roots, grew pale mushrooms and root-fruit in the dark, drew water from deep springs and lit their streets with lanterns fed by the faint glow of the Tree's magic. Their children were born below and learned the Oath before they learned to read. Over the centuries, the camp became Cavelor: small, orderly, and completely devoted to its task.

The guardians never stopped watching. Cavelor's Wardens of the Seal walk the deep passages around the prison in shifts, and have done so without a single gap for the whole of the kingdom's history. Its scholars keep careful records of every tremor and every change in the seal's glow, written in great ledgers that go back to the founding.

docs.title: Rediscovery
docs.text:
For generations, Cavelor had almost no contact with the rest of the kingdom. Then, fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition reached its halls. The explorers were astonished to find the legend alive; the guardians were just as astonished to learn how completely the surface had forgotten them.

It was a joyful meeting, and a terrible one. Within days of that first contact, the expedition's explorers, pushing deeper than the guardians advised, opened the rift that damaged the seal. Cavelor's ledgers recorded the change at once. For fifty years since, the guardians have watched the seal grow weaker, and they have tried, with growing urgency, to make the surface understand what that means.

docs.title: Cultural Identity
docs.text:
Cavelor's people live by responsibility, vigilance, discipline and endurance. They keep the traditions of the first guardians and guard the records of the Balrog, the ancient battle and the magic that holds the prison shut. Every adult in Cavelor serves a turn as a Warden.

Their duty is a solemn one, but Cavelor is not a gloomy or oppressive place. Its people have built a real community with a life of its own: they are close-knit and fiercely loyal, quick to laugh among themselves, and deeply curious about the bright world above, which many of them have only recently seen for the first time.

Cavelor is still very much its own place, but since its rediscovery it has been part of the same united kingdom, and its people are as proud of Wonder Kingdom as anyone on the surface. They just know better than most what it might cost to keep it.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Cavelor.

Design notes

New with this page: guardians from all four peoples, the Oath Below, the Wardens of the Seal and their ledgers, and the rift being opened days after the expedition reached Cavelor.

docs.title: Fairy Forest
docs.text:
The Magical Woodland

Fairy Forest is a settlement hidden among ancient trees, where enchanted plants grow, strange creatures wander and the air hums with magic. It is the historic home of the Magicians, one of the four founding peoples.

docs.title: The Listening Woods
docs.text:
The Magicians did not choose Fairy Forest so much as find it. Long before the Age of Division, the first of them came to these woods because magic gathered here more thickly than anywhere else on Veligor, like water collecting in a valley. They believed, and still believe, that the forest's roots reach all the way to the World Tree's, and that the Tree's magic flows outward through the soil and comes up again here.

They learned magic by listening: to the trees, to the wind, to the creatures that lived among them. Their first homes were built into living trunks and branches, shaped by coaxing the trees to grow rather than by cutting them, and the oldest of those homes are still lived in today.

docs.title: Keepers of the Tree
docs.text:
Through the Age of Division, the Magicians guarded the forest and, above all, the World Tree. Any attempt to cut, claim or exploit a place of power was met by Magician resistance, and that was the root of their long alliance with the Savages, who had no love for outside rulers either.

In the Balrog War, it was the Magicians of Fairy Forest who understood what the Balrog was enough to know it could not be destroyed, and who designed the great seal that holds it beneath the World Tree. The knowledge of how that seal was made has been one of the forest's most closely guarded secrets ever since. Since the expedition damaged it, the forest's scholars have been studying old records day and night, trying to understand how it might be strengthened.

docs.title: The Children Arrive
docs.text:
Fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition found a mysterious people of magical beings living high in the upper reaches of the World Tree. They came to be known as the Children of the Tree.

After that first meeting, the Children slowly came down from the Tree and settled in Fairy Forest, perhaps because its magic felt most like home. The forest welcomed them as family. They have since become part of its community and made friends across the kingdom, and their presence gives the forest much of its unique magic.

docs.title: Environment and Culture
docs.text:
The people of Fairy Forest live close to both magic and nature. Magical learning, care for the living forest and the study of supernatural wonders are at the heart of who they are. The settlement does not stand apart from the woods; its homes and gathering places are woven into the forest itself, linked by branch-bridges, lantern-lit paths and stairways that spiral around the trunks.

The forest's schools teach magic to anyone with the gift, from any town in the kingdom. Its people take only what the forest can spare, and they will gently but firmly stop any visitor who tries to take more.

The forest has its own friends in the wider kingdom, too. The Brenna of Midbarium have been welcome here since the days when the Savages and the Magicians were allies, and the friendship has outlasted the war that made it.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Fairy Forest.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by MapleStory's Ellinia. New with this page: magic gathering in the forest through the World Tree's roots, homes grown from living trees, and the Magicians designing the seal. The nature, appearance, abilities and origins of the Children of the Tree are still to be decided.

docs.title: Goa Harbour
docs.text:
The Wilderness Harbour

Goa Harbour is a port on the far side of Veligor from Bain Harbour. It feels like a little of Midbarium and a little of Fairy Forest, with highland ruggedness and woodland magic meeting the sea.

docs.title: Where the Mountains Meet the Sea
docs.text: The coast around Goa Harbour is wild: cliffs that drop straight into the water, forests that run down to the shore, and a single deep inlet cut between them. During the Age of Division, both Savages and Magicians came to that inlet. Savage hunters came down from the hills for the fishing, and Magicians came for the sea-herbs and the strange tides, which they believed were moved by the same magic that flowed through the forests. Being allies, they shared it, and a mixed camp grew up on the shore.

docs.title: The Sea Wardens
docs.text:
The camp gave the town its oldest tradition. The tides in the inlet are fast and treacherous, and the first families learned to read them the way Magicians read the forest. They called themselves wardens of the sea, and to this day, Goa Harbour's pilots guide every ship through the inlet, and no captain sails in without one.

The name Goa is said to come from an old Savage word for "the gap", the narrow gap between the cliffs where the inlet opens to the sea.

docs.title: After the Founding
docs.text: When the kingdom was founded, Goa Harbour opened to the whole island. Timber from its forests and furs and wool from the highlands went out by sea, and travellers began to come for the wild coast and the strange, half-magical town on it. It never grew as large or as busy as Bain Harbour, and its people prefer it that way.

docs.title: Environment and Identity
docs.text:
Goa Harbour is rougher and wilder than Bain Harbour, shaped by the mountains, forests and rocky shores around it. Its houses are built of timber and stone and climb the cliffs above the water, joined by rope bridges and carved stairways much like Midbarium's, while lanterns of the forest's making light its quays at night.

Its people keep proud seafaring traditions, along with the independent spirit and touch of magic of the neighboring regions. They are adventurous and welcoming, and the town is unlike any other on the island. It is also a natural home for adventurers: since the Age of Disturbance began, the wild coast and forests around it have filled with monsters, and Goa Harbour's people have never been the sort to wait for help.

docs.title: Independence
docs.text:
Goa Harbour is not Midbarium's port, nor Fairy Forest's. It has its own people, traditions and history, and its resemblance to those towns is cultural, not political. It is led by its First Warden, the most respected of its pilots, chosen by the others.

Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour are not rivals. Both are peaceful, prosperous parts of Wonder Kingdom, and every summer their sailors race each other all the way around Veligor.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Goa Harbour.

Design notes

New with this page: the shared Savage and Magician camp, the sea wardens and the First Warden, the meaning of the name "Goa", and the summer race with Bain Harbour.

docs.title: Kaldemor
docs.text:
The Town of Joyful Craftsmanship

Kaldemor is a cheerful pastoral town set among fertile fields, rolling hills and green countryside, "the greenest town this side of the old forest", as its mayor likes to say. Its heart is joyful craftsmanship: its people love making things with their own hands, growing their own food and living well together. Just under three hundred people live there, not counting the snails.

docs.title: One Seed
docs.text:
Every child in Kaldemor knows how the town began. Long ago, a traveller crossing the eastern meadows planted a single seed and slept beside it for the night. In the morning, the seed had become a tree taller than a tower.

People came from all over to see it, and some of them never left. They built their homes around the great tree, and then in it: the great treehouse behind the town square is the oldest building in Kaldemor. Nobody remembers the traveller's name, but the town still lives by the saying the story left behind: every great town starts with one seed.

Whether the seed came from the World Tree, as the Magicians of Fairy Forest suspect, nobody can say. But the soil around Kaldemor has been strangely generous ever since.

docs.title: Mushroom Houses and Windmills
docs.text:
That generous soil grows mushrooms big enough to live in, and Kaldemor's settlers did exactly that. The town's famous mushroom houses are real mushrooms, hollowed out, fitted with doors and windows, and painted in bright colors. They grow a little every spring, and their owners simply add another room.

The early settlers were mostly Commons: farmers, carpenters, potters and bakers. They planted the fields and orchards, raised a windmill farm in the park, and built workshops wherever there was room. When the Royal Road was laid from Selsior to the east, Kaldemor became the last stop before the eastern countryside, and its markets grew busy with travellers.

docs.title: The Clock Tower
docs.text:
The town's other landmark is the clock tower in the park. It was raised by the whole town together, a gift from every family and every workshop, and its bell has kept Kaldemor's time ever since. The terrace oven in the market was built the same year, by Rosa the baker's grandmother, and it has not gone cold since.

The clock stopped once, not long ago, when a Shroom from the woods carried off its great gear. The whole town held its breath until the gear came back and the bell rang again.

docs.title: The Town Today
docs.text:
Kaldemor is led by its mayor, chosen by the townspeople. Mayor Tobin has held the post for thirty years and knows every family by name. The town square sits in the middle, with the Market to the east for potions, weapons and bread, and the Park to the west with its clock tower and windmills.

Beyond the town lie the fields, hills and woods where young warriors learn their trade, and lately there has been plenty to learn on. Snails eat the gardens, Shrooms raid the woods, and something huge has settled in a hollow past the woods: a giant snail the townsfolk call the Snail King. The town's park ranger and drillmaster keep a close watch on the wilds, and they are always glad of help.

docs.title: Architecture and Environment
docs.text: Kaldemor is a town of colorful wooden houses and cozy cottages, mushroom houses and treehouses, workshops and gardens, barns and welcoming village greens. Beyond it stretch meadows, farmland, orchards, gentle hills and patches of woodland. It is a sunny, colorful place that seems to invite visitors in.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
The people of Kaldemor value creativity, practical know-how, friendliness, cooperation and the quiet satisfaction of work done well. Traditional crafts are part of everyday life: woodworking, carpentry, pottery, baking and farming all shape who the town is.

Kaldemor is no poor backwater. It is a prosperous, happy town whose people love the life they have made. Where Selsior stands for the excitement and variety of the great city, Kaldemor stands for the joy of creating, growing and belonging to a close-knit community.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Kaldemor.

In the game

Kaldemor is in the game today. See Kaldemor in the world guide for its maps, NPCs, quests and hunting grounds.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by the bright, welcoming character of MapleStory's Henesys. The seed story, the treehouse, the mushroom houses, the clock tower, Mayor Tobin and the Snail King come from the game itself. New with this page: the guess that the seed came from the World Tree, and the clock tower being raised by the whole town.

docs.title: Midbarium
docs.text:
The Highland Settlement

Midbarium is a rugged, rural mountain town and the ancestral home of the Savages' culture. It sits high in Veligor's dry uplands, among red-rock peaks, sheer cliffs, deep canyons and steep highland trails, and its people grew strong learning to live with them.

docs.title: The Land
docs.text:
The highlands around Midbarium are a hard, beautiful country. Rain is scarce, the sun is fierce, and the wind carries red dust down the canyons for days at a time. Above the town rise wind-carved mesas and bare stone spires; below it, dry riverbeds wind through rocky valleys dotted with caves, hardy scrub and the odd twisted tree. Nights are cold and clear, and the stars over the plateau are famous across the kingdom.

Life here follows the land. There are no grand fields like Kaldemor's. Instead, families farm small stone terraces on the slopes, watered by springs and carefully kept cisterns, and they drive herds of goats and other hardy beasts between the high pastures and the valley floors as the seasons turn. Many Midbarians live not in the town itself but in scattered homesteads and camps across the highlands, coming in to trade, to settle disputes and to celebrate.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Midbarium is built into the mountainside. Its houses are thick-walled and earthen-red, made of stone and sun-dried clay that keep out the heat of the day and hold warmth through the night. Heavy timber beams carry the roofs of the great halls, and terraces, carved stairways and swaying rope-and-plank bridges join the levels of the town across the cliffs.

Out in the highlands, herding families live in sturdy hide tents and stone shelters that can be moved or rebuilt with the seasons. Painted standards and carved totems mark the camps of each family.

docs.title: The Four Families
docs.text: Midbarium is not governed like Selsior. Its people belong to four great families, clans bound by blood, oath and shared history, and each family follows a chieftain.

docs.title: The Kragvar
docs.text: The stone-cutters. The Kragvar built Midbarium. Their ancestors cut the first terraces, raised the great hall and carved the stairways that climb the cliffs, and Kragvar masons still keep every wall and bridge in the town standing. In the Age of Division they were the hardest of the Savage warriors, and in the Balrog War they stood in the front line. Kragvar songs claim that some of their greatest fighters never came home from that war, but stayed beneath the World Tree to keep watch. The family keeps the council fire in the great hall burning, and counts that as its proudest duty.

docs.title: The Tolmach
docs.text: The herders. The Tolmach are the wanderers of the highlands. Most of the family still lives in hide tents and moves with its herds between the high pastures and the valley floors, as it has for longer than anyone remembers. They know every old path through the canyons and every spring that runs in a dry year, and that knowledge kept the Savages alive through the long wars. After the founding, it was Tolmach guides who first led traders from Kaldemor and Selsior up into the mountains, and they still bring most of the town's wool, hides and cheese down to market.

docs.title: The Uskari
docs.text: The hunters. The Uskari live along the canyon rims, and they are the best trackers, climbers and scouts in Veligor. They once hunted the great beasts of the plateau, and in the old wars they were the eyes of the Savage armies. Since the Age of Disturbance began, the Uskari have taken on a new duty: they patrol the highland trails, drive off the monsters that come up from the canyons, and see travelers safely from one camp to the next. Many young Uskari leave home to become adventurers.

docs.title: The Brenna
docs.text: The keepers. The Brenna are Midbarium's healers, storytellers and drummers. They know the highland herbs and how to set a broken bone, and they keep the memory of the families: the long songs that name every chieftain and every Old One back to the Age of Division, recited at every gathering. When the Savages and Magicians were allies, it was Brenna envoys who walked to the forests to talk with them, and the family still has old friends in Fairy Forest. The Brenna host every choosing, and their drums call the families together.

docs.title: The Chieftains and the Old One
docs.text:
A chieftain is not simply born to the role. When a chieftain dies, their family gathers around its fire and chooses a new one from among its own people, for strength, wisdom and fairness. A chieftain is expected to lead from the front: to walk the hardest trail first, to judge disputes fairly, to protect the herds and to look after the weakest members of the family.

Above the four chieftains stands one leader for all of Midbarium, whom everyone calls the Old One. The name is a title of respect, not a description: an Old One can be any age. The Old One is chosen the same way. When the Old One dies, the four families come together at the great hall, around the fire that is never allowed to go out, and choose the next. By custom, no family may hold the title twice in a row, so each Old One owes the role to all four families, not to their own.

The chieftains meet in council with the Old One to settle matters that touch the whole town. Debates are long and loud, but once the Old One closes the council, every family stands by its decision. Within Wonder Kingdom, the Old One speaks for Midbarium, and the families are as loyal to the kingdom as any lord in the capital.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
Midbarium stands for strength, resilience, independence and respect for the ancestors. Its people admire anyone who overcomes hardship, and they guard the knowledge handed down by earlier generations: the old paths through the canyons, where water can be found in a dry year, and the stories of the four families.

Hospitality is sacred in the highlands, where a traveler turned away might not survive the night. Anyone who comes to a Midbarian fire in peace is given water, food and a place to sleep, no questions asked. Feasts, storytelling, contests of strength and long nights of drumming and song mark the families' gatherings.

For all its rugged looks, Midbarium is not hostile, primitive or grim, and it holds nothing against outsiders. Today it is a peaceful, welcoming town whose people are proud of both their ancestral traditions and their place in Wonder Kingdom.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Midbarium.

Design notes

The geography and look are inspired by MapleStory's Perion. Midbarium is rural and mountainous, ruled by the chieftains of four families and the Old One, with a dry highland and desert feel. It should draw on highland, canyon and steppe cultures, not on Middle Eastern or Arabian desert cultures. Still open: who the current chieftains and Old One are, and how a family decides between rivals when it chooses a chieftain.

docs.title: Selsior
docs.text:
The City of Everything

Selsior is the capital of Wonder Kingdom and by far the largest city on Veligor. It is a bustling fantasy metropolis: crowded, noisy, endlessly busy and remarkably diverse. People call it the City of Everything, and they mean it. Its residents trade, craft, teach, study, perform, govern and do a thousand other things besides, in marketplaces and workshops, schools and theatres, taverns and quiet residential lanes.

docs.title: The Treaty Field
docs.text:
Before there was a city, there was a field. When the Balrog had been sealed away, the leaders of the four peoples needed somewhere to meet that belonged to none of them. They chose a broad, empty meadow on the island's central plain, a day's ride from the World Tree, where the armies of all four peoples had camped together during the last months of the war. There, under open sky, they signed the founding treaty.

The field never emptied again. Envoys stayed to make the treaty work, traders came to sell to the envoys, craftsmen came to build for the traders, and within a generation the camp had become a town. The four peoples agreed to make it the seat of the new kingdom, precisely because it had never belonged to any of them.

docs.title: Growing Into a Capital
docs.text:
The Aristocrats brought the skills of building and government, and the early city looked much like their old fortress towns: thick walls, a stone keep and straight streets. But the Commons filled it with markets and workshops, Magicians founded its first schools, and Savage clans built halls for their envoys and their feasts. Over the centuries, Selsior outgrew every wall built around it, and the old quarters grew into the winding maze they are today.

The spot where the treaty was signed is now the central plaza. The Great Bell stands there on its dais, cast from metal given by all four peoples. It rings only when a new monarch is crowned, and the guards will tell anyone who asks that it rings for no one else.

docs.title: The Palace and the Crown
docs.text:
The kingdom's monarch rules from the palace at the head of the plaza, where the throne hall's red carpet runs up the palace steps. The crown's task, as Selsior's people like to say, is not to command the kingdom but to keep it together: to uphold the founding treaty, settle disputes between towns, keep the roads safe and speak for Wonder Kingdom as a whole. Each town keeps its own leaders and customs, from Kaldemor's mayor to Midbarium's Old One.

The Royal Vault beneath the palace keeps the kingdom's treasures and records, and its keepers will also guard the belongings of any citizen who asks.

docs.title: The Knights' Court and the Royal Guard
docs.text: The Royal Guard keeps the peace in the capital and on the royal roads. Its home is the Knights' Court, where recruits drill from dawn and its captains train warriors in the way of the sword. The Guard is open to anyone from any town who can pass its trials, and since the Age of Disturbance began, it has had no shortage of work. Its ranks run from the Swordsman to the Swordmaster and the Grand Swordmaster, and old books name one more, the Sword Saint, earned by very few.

docs.title: The Crown Market
docs.text: The Crown Market is the busiest place on Veligor. Here, Kaldemor's bread sits beside Midbarium's wool, Bain Harbour's fish beside Fairy Forest's herbs, and Urbanograd's strange inventions beside the finest blades in the kingdom. Its shopkeepers, apothecaries, weaponsmiths and armourers serve adventurers from every town.

docs.title: The Gate
docs.text: The city's great gate faces the Royal Road, which runs east past the Greenwood to Kaldemor. Gate guards greet every traveller, and taxis wait at the gate stand to carry visitors between the capital and the other towns.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Selsior is a classic medieval fantasy city. Timber-framed houses stand on stone foundations under brightly colored roofs, towers rise over the skyline, and cobblestone streets run between the neighborhoods.

At its heart lie broad avenues, great public squares, the palace and the city's most important civic spaces. Around them sprawl dense old quarters that grew without a plan: winding streets, narrow passages, hidden courtyards, crowded homes, little local markets, and skywalks that cross above the streets.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
Selsior is cheerful, sociable and full of energy. Street performers draw crowds on every corner, dancers turn in the plaza, festivals fill the squares, and there always seems to be something to celebrate. The city is busy not only because people work there, but because its people love city life and throw themselves into it.

Folk from every corner of Wonder Kingdom live side by side in Selsior, and nobody thinks that strange. More than anywhere else, the capital shows what the founding of the kingdom achieved: prosperity, cooperation and a shared identity, with room for every kind of life and ambition.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Selsior.

In the game

Selsior is in the game today. See Selsior in the world guide for its maps, NPCs and shops.

Design notes

Classic medieval fantasy architecture. Joyful, bustling and cosmopolitan. New with this page: the Treaty Field and the treaty signed where the plaza now stands, the Great Bell cast from all four peoples' metal, and the crown's role as keeper of the treaty. Still open: who the current monarch is, and how monarchs are chosen.

docs.title: Urbanograd
docs.text:
The Town of Societal Rebels

Urbanograd is a city unlike any other on Veligor. It was founded 100 years ago, long after the four peoples had united, so its identity has nothing to do with the old wars. It grew up inside the kingdom, built by people who wanted to live their own way: free to express themselves and free of the expectations of ordinary society. Over the century since, it has grown a counterculture all its own.

docs.title: A Kingdom That Had Settled Down
docs.text:
A century ago, Wonder Kingdom had known peace for so long that peace had grown comfortable, and comfort had grown habits. In Selsior, the old guilds decided who could practice which trade, who could sell in which square and which songs could be sung in the theatres. Families expected their children to follow the trade they were born into. Even Kaldemor, for all its warmth, had firm ideas about what a good, honest life looked like.

None of this was cruel. It was simply how things had always been done, and most people were happy with it. But a restless few were not: painters whose work the galleries called vulgar, musicians who played too loud and too fast, tinkerers whose inventions no guild would license, young people who wanted to dress, love and live in ways their elders did not understand. In the capital, they gathered in cellars, rooftops and back-alley taverns, and they began to talk about leaving.

docs.title: The Long Walk
docs.text:
The spark was a small thing. When the theatre guild of Selsior banned a play by Juna Marrow, a young playwright whose comedy poked fun at the city's grandees, she performed it anyway, on a cart in the middle of the market square, to the biggest crowd the square had seen in years. The guild had her cart hauled away. That night, she told her friends she was done asking permission, and that she meant to build a town where nobody would ever have to.

A few weeks later, about three hundred people walked out of Selsior's gates together: artists, musicians, craftspeople without a guild, inventors, wanderers, and plenty who simply wanted something different. Others joined them along the road from Kaldemor, the harbours and the highlands. They called themselves the Walkers, and the day they left is still celebrated in Urbanograd as Walkout Day.

docs.title: The Empty City
docs.text:
The Walkers did not build Urbanograd from nothing. They settled in Old Grad, the ruins of a walled stronghold built by the Aristocrats in the Age of Division and abandoned after the founding of the kingdom, when nobody needed fortresses anymore. For generations it had stood empty: crumbling towers, roofless halls and a maze of narrow streets slowly being taken back by weeds.

The Walkers saw something else in it. They patched the roofs with whatever they could find, strung lanterns between the towers, painted every bare wall and turned the old barracks into workshops, theatres and homes. They added the name the city still carries: Urbanograd, roughly "the city of Grad", half a joke about the grand old fortress and half a promise of what it would become.

The first winters were hard. The Walkers knew a great deal about art and very little about farming, and more than one of them went home. Those who stayed learned to trade their crafts, music and inventions for food, and travelers began to come just to see the strange new town.

docs.title: The Kingdom's Answer
docs.text:
Not everyone was pleased. Some in Selsior called the Walkers deserters, and a few guild masters asked the crown to send them home. The question went all the way to the royal court.

The answer came from the founding treaty itself. It promised that every people of Veligor could live together in peace, whatever their culture. The court ruled that the promise did not only protect the four peoples who had signed it, but any people who chose to live differently, so long as they kept the kingdom's peace and laws. Urbanograd was recognized as a town of Wonder Kingdom, with the same rights as any other.

That ruling, known in Urbanograd as the Open Charter, is the reason the city exists as it does today. Its people have never forgotten that the kingdom chose to welcome them, and that is why their rebellion has always been about how they live, never about overturning the realm that let them.

docs.title: A Century of Urbanograd
docs.text:
Over the next hundred years, Old Grad filled up. Each generation built on top of the last, so the city grew upward rather than outward: houses stacked on houses, bridges between rooftops, staircases that lead to three different places at once. New arrivals kept coming from every town on Veligor, bringing their own crafts and ideas and making the city ever more varied.

Today Urbanograd is a busy, noisy, colorful town, famous for its music, its street art, its workshops and its night markets. Juna Marrow's play is performed in the main square every Walkout Day, on a cart, as it was the first time.

docs.title: Cultural Identity
docs.text:
Urbanograd is famous as the home of societal rebels. Its people prize individuality, creativity, unconventional thinking, free expression and the right to live differently. The city draws anyone who loves alternative lifestyles and unusual art, music and fashion.

The city has no lord or chieftain. Matters that concern everyone are talked out at the Open Table, a long gathering in the old fortress's great hall where anyone who lives in Urbanograd may speak. It is loud, slow and often funny, and its people would not have it any other way.

But its people are not revolutionaries. They have no wish to unsettle the kingdom, topple its institutions or quarrel with their neighbors. Their rebellion is cultural and personal, not political.

docs.title: Relationship with Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
Urbanograd is a full and proud part of Wonder Kingdom. Its people respect the kingdom and get along well with every other community, and the rest of Veligor accepts the city's unusual character. Its people are understood, not distrusted. Even Selsior's guilds, which once wanted the Walkers brought home, now send their apprentices to Urbanograd to see what new things its workshops have come up with.

Urbanograd shows that the kingdom's founding promise reaches further than peace between the original four peoples. Wonder Kingdom also welcomes communities that invent entirely new ways of living.

People

Everyone who lives here in the first release: People of Urbanograd.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by MapleStory's Kerning City. Juna Marrow, the Walkers, Old Grad, the Open Charter and the Open Table are new with this page. Still open: where on Veligor Urbanograd lies, and what the city looks like beyond its fortress core.

  • Hale's Bounty (gives)

Dialogue
  • I look after the park gate and the meadow beyond it. What can I do for you, Player?
    • Choice: What is out in the meadow?
    • Choice: Any advice for a newcomer?
    • Choice: Take me to the Snail King's hollow.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Mostly snails: green ones near the town, blue ones and red ones a little farther. They are slow and harmless enough, but they nibble.
  • East of the town square, past the portal, the meadow opens up. Hunt a few and you will learn how a fight goes.
  • Press Ctrl to swing, and keep a potion on a key. Whatever the snails leave behind, Z picks it up.
  • Then keep your potions close and your feet moving, Player. Jump the red marks, and do not stay still when it sweeps. I will open the way.
  • Walk safe, Player.

docs.title: Lia
docs.text:
Town Guide

Where Kaldemor Services Quests

Welcome to Kaldemor, Player!

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "New in town? Ask me anything!"
  • "Press Space near someone to talk to them."
  • "The market is just east of here."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Welcome Home (gives)
Dialogue
  • Hi, Player! I show newcomers around Kaldemor. Ask me anything!
    • Choice: Where am I?
    • Choice: What is there to do here?
    • Choice: Anything new in town?
    • Choice: Am I ready for the fields?
    • Choice: How do I...?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Of course! What would you like to know?
    • Choice: ...move and fight?
    • Choice: ...see how strong I am?
    • Choice: ...learn and use skills?
    • Choice: ...carry and wear things?
    • Choice: ...keep track of my quests?
    • Choice: Never mind.
  • Walk with the arrow keys and jump with Alt. Up takes a portal or climbs a ladder, and Down with Alt drops through a ledge.
  • Swing with Ctrl, pick up what monsters leave behind with Z, and talk to people with Space or a click. Every key can be changed with the backslash key.
  • Press S to open your stat window: your level, HP and MP, and the strength, dexterity and the rest that decide how hard you hit.
  • Every level gives you ability points to spend there. A warrior puts most of them into STR.
  • Press K for your skills. Each level from the second one gives you skill points, and a click on the + puts one into a skill.
  • A skill has a key of its own, and costs MP each time you use it. Blue potions bring the MP back.
  • Press I for your inventory: four tabs, one for what you wear, drink, collect and sit on. Double-click a potion to drink it.
  • Press E for what you wear: double-click a piece of equipment to put it on, and a worn one to take it off.
  • Press Q for your quest log: what you can take up, what you are doing, and what you have done. Pick a quest to read its story and its rewards.
  • The quests you follow are listed on the right of the screen with how far you are. Click one to open it in the log.
  • This is the town square of Kaldemor. The big treehouse behind us is the oldest building in town.
  • The people here are friendly. Say hello to everyone: press Space near someone, or click them!
  • Visit the Market to the east for potions and gear. When you feel strong, the fields beyond the town are full of monsters to practice on.
  • People with a light bulb over their head have a job for you. Helping them is a good way to learn your way around!
  • Oh, yes! The clock tower in the park has stopped. Nobody can say when it will tick again.
  • Old Ewan, the clockkeeper, has been up there for days. Maybe he would like some company.
  • You carry (how many you carry) Red Potions - good. Snails nibble, and a potion mends it. Drink one with its key before it gets serious!
  • I would take some Red Potions along first: you carry (how many you carry). Bram sells them in the market, east of here.
  • Have fun, Player!

docs.title: Quill
docs.text:
Drillmaster

Where Kaldemor Park Services Run: Kaldemor Gauntlet

Chin up, Player. Eyes front.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Footwork wins more fights than muscle."
  • "Again! Once more, from the top!"
  • "A course does not care how brave you feel."
Dialogue
  • I drill those who want to be tested, Player. Spikes, rocks, platforms that will not wait for you, and a yard full of things that bite. What will it be?
    • Choice: What is the Gauntlet?
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Three stages, one after the other. First the yard: whatever I turn loose, you beat down. Then the hanging course: gather the star shards and reach the far ledge before the clock runs out. Then the last stand: hold out for a full minute.
  • Fall, flee or run out of time, and it is over. Come back and I will send you in again, no waiting. Potions are allowed. Scrolls are not.
  • Not yet, Player. Come back at level 10 and I will put you through it.
  • Good. Keep your potions close and your feet moving, Player. In you go.
  • Walk tall, Player.

docs.title: Rhys
docs.text:
Captain of the Royal Guard

Stand tall, Player.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• The Swordsman's Trial (gives)
  • The Swordmaster's Trial (gives)
  • The Grand Swordmaster's Trial (gives)
  • The Sword Saint's Trial (gives)
Dialogue
  • I am Captain Rhys. I train warriors of the Royal Guard in the Swordsman's way.
    • Choice: What is a Swordsman?
    • Choice: Can I advance?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • A Warrior who has learned patience. The Swordsman fights with fast, controlled cuts, where other Warriors only swing hard.
  • It is the first step on the Swordmaster's road, the one a Warrior takes from level 30. The road goes on: the Swordmaster from level 70, the Grand Swordmaster from level 120, and last the Sword Saint from level 160.
  • Not yet, Player. Come back at level 30, and we shall see whether you are ready for the Guard's trial.
  • You have the strength for it, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the Guard's trial.
  • You are one of us already, Player, and the road goes on: the Swordmaster. Come back at level 70, and the Guard will set you its next trial.
  • Level seventy, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the Swordmaster's trial.
  • A Swordmaster, and a fine one. There is one step more, the Grand Swordmaster. Come back at level 120.
  • Level one hundred and twenty, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the last trial.
  • A Grand Swordmaster stands at the top of the Guard, Player, yet the old books name one rank more, the Sword Saint. Come back at level 160.
  • Level one hundred and sixty, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the old test, the Sword Saint's.
  • There is no rank above yours that I can give, Player. What the sword can teach you now, it teaches on the road.
  • Keep your guard up.

docs.title: Rosa

Where Kaldemor Market Services Quests

docs.title: Says

docs.title: Quests

• Rosa's Recipe (gives)
  • A Loaf for Bram (gives)
  • A Pot for Rosa (gives)
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player, the one who found my spores! Come in, come in, wipe your boots.
  • Player! I saved you the heel of the loaf, it is the best part. Sit a moment, the oven is warm.
  • My dear Player, there you are. The bakery is as much yours as mine, you know. Take what you like.
  • Welcome to my bakery, Player! What can I do for you?
    • Choice: What do you bake?
    • Choice: Is business good?
    • Choice: Tell me about your oven.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Bread, mostly: round loaves, long loaves, and my mushroom bread, which the whole town swears by. The terrace oven has not gone cold in years.
  • The secret is in the spores. Do not tell anyone I said so.
  • Oh, it is lively! Half the market comes up my steps before noon, and the other half comes after.
  • Oh, it is lively! And half of them ask after you, Player. You have a name in Kaldemor now, did you know? The mayor's own bread comes from this oven.
  • You want the oven's story? My grandmother built it with her own hands, brick by brick, the year the clock tower was raised. She said a bakery without a warm oven is only a shop.
  • I have never told that to a customer. Somehow you do not feel like one anymore, Player.
  • Come back hungry, Player!

  • A cab runs between towns with a taxi stand, never into the wilds. You have to have walked to a town before I will drive you there.
  • Mind the road!

docs.title: Tobe
docs.text:
Recruit

Where Knights' Court

I read about swordsmanship. The book did not mention how heavy swords are.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Step, strike, step, strike..."
  • "The manual says the third cut is the hard one."

docs.title: Tobin
docs.text:
Mayor of Kaldemor

Where Kaldemor Services Quests

Welcome to Kaldemor, Player!

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Lovely weather today."
  • "Have you met Lia, our guide?"
  • "That treehouse has outlived three mayors, and I am the third."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Welcome Home (completes)
  • Settling In (gives)
  • Snail Trouble (gives)
  • Shells for the Mayor (completes)
  • Strength of a Warrior (gives)
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player! Lia told you about the clock tower, did she? Old Ewan has been fretting about it for days.
  • Welcome to Kaldemor, the greenest town this side of the old forest. What can I do for you?
    • Choice: Tell me about Kaldemor.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Guess how many people live here.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Kaldemor grew up around the great treehouse behind me. The mushroom houses came later - the soil here grows them big enough to live in!
  • West of the square is the Park, with the clock tower and the old windmill farm. East is the Market: potions, weapons, bread, all of it.
  • Walk through the glowing portals with the up arrow to go between them.
  • I'm Tobin, mayor of this town for thirty years now. Would you like to hear how Kaldemor began?
  • Long ago a traveller planted a single seed in this meadow and slept under it for a night. In the morning it was a tree taller than a tower.
  • People came to see it, and some never left. That traveller's name is lost, but we still say: every great town starts with one seed.
  • Another time, then. Old men always have time for stories.
  • A guess, is it? Go on: how many people live in Kaldemor, would you say?
  • N, you say? Not bad, Player! There are just under three hundred of us - not counting the snails.
  • Take care out there, Player. Come back any time!

docs.text:
Armourer

Where Crown Market Services Shop: Vessa's Armour

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Mail, helms and boots, fitted while you wait."
  • "Armour is only heavy until the first hit lands on it."

Orin's Wife

Where Kaldemor Park

Hello, dear. Orin tells the same stories, but I never tire of them.

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "Orin, you are shouting again."
  • "I knit caps for every child in Kaldemor. Some even wear them."
  • "The park is nicest in the afternoon."

docs.title: Professions
docs.text:
Gathering professions take materials from nodes in the fields; making professions turn them into items.

Professions go up to level 99. Ranks: Novice (1), Apprentice (20), Journeyman (40), Expert (60), Master (80).

docs.title: Story quests
docs.text: Quest Level From Summary Welcome Home 1 Lia Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin. Settling In 1 Tobin Tobin wants you to see the Market and meet Bram, the potion seller. Snail Trouble 2 Tobin Snails are eating the town's gardens. Thin them out in the meadow, then see Ranger Hale at the park gate. Shells for the Mayor 2 Hale Mayor Tobin collects snail shells for the new fence. Bring him 15 Green Snail Shells. Strength of a Warrior 3 Tobin Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve. The Clock Stopped 4 Ewan The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back. The Snail King 12 Hale Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find. The Swordsman's Trial 30 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 30 of its monsters and bring back 5 trial seals. The Swordmaster's Trial 70 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters. The Grand Swordmaster's Trial 120 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters. The Sword Saint's Trial 160 Rhys Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters.
